1	# VPS 每人／每裝置憑證與生命週期管理
2	
3	**Status**: P?
4	**Effort**: L
5	**Related**: `TODO.md` · server deployment/export · historical analytics
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	2026-09-22：歷史流量分析需要辨識來源。現有 deployment 產生單一 UUID／密碼，
10	多人共用時，來源 IP 是網路端點而非可靠的人或裝置身分。第一版 analytics 沿用
11	目前憑證，顯示觀測來源和未知歸因；憑證管理另外實作，避免分析安裝偷偷換掉帳號。
12	
13	## Investigation
14	
15	- VLESS／VMess 支援同 inbound 多個使用者：UUID 是憑證，`email` 是伺服器端
16	  識別／統計標籤，不必是真實信箱。以部署版本確認 `clients`／`users` 相容格式。
17	- Xray `HandlerService.AlterInbound` 的 AddUser／RemoveUser 修改執行中狀態；
18	  沒有自動寫回持久配置的契約，不能只呼叫 API 就宣稱撤銷在重啟後仍有效。
19	- 原始碼中 RemoveUser 移除認證資料，不能據此保證已認證的長連線或 multiplex
20	  transport 立即停止。若以重啟確保失效，須顯示同服務其他使用者也會中斷。
21	- VLESS／VMess 的非空 email 不可重複，查找不區分大小寫。新舊 UUID 重疊輪替
22	  需不同 credential labels，再映射至同一穩定 person/device ID。
23	- Hysteria2 有多使用者認證與按 ID kick API；kick 必須配合拒絕重新認證。
24	  其撤銷契約不同，不能直接套用 Xray 實作。
25	
26	## Decision
27	
28	先規劃持久設定為準的版本：registry 是 users 清單的唯一擁有者，生成 server
29	配置及指定裝置 client profile。保留舊憑證為明確 legacy entry。新增、撤銷、
30	輪替皆經驗證、差異預覽、套用與讀回；新增憑證不進一般日誌／analytics 報表。
31	
32	動態 API 更新列後續，須先解決持久化、重啟 reconciliation 和未知寫入結果。
33	提供穩定裝置 ID、獨立隨機 UUID、版本化 credential ID；不把來源 IP 當成 owner。
34	
35	## Acceptance and remaining decisions
36	
37	- A／B 可獨立發放、匯出及統計；撤銷 A 後新認證失敗，B 正常。
38	- 分別驗證新握手、已建立 TCP、UDP、multiplex 的撤銷行為。
39	- 輪替後新憑證成功、舊憑證失敗；重啟與重新生成配置不復活已撤銷憑證。
40	- 套用失敗與不確定結果保留恢復資料；原始憑證不出現在摘要、診斷或一般 JSON。
41	- 實作前決定第一版是否支援重疊輪替，以及哪些 core 版本可免重啟更新。
42

19			scope = "SSH noninteractive process"
20		}
21		result := HostEvidence{Protocol: 1, Scope: scope, Capabilities: []Capability{}, DNS: DNSResult{Source: "host native resolver", Addresses: []string{}}, Routes: []RouteEvidence{}, Requests: []RequestEvidence{}}
22		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 22*time.Second)
23		defer cancel()
24		input, err := json.Marshal(request)
25		if err != nil {
26			return result, errors.New("cannot encode host evidence request")
27		}
28		data, err := connection.ExecutePython(ctx, sshHost, hostProbeScript, input, 128*1024)
29		if err != nil {
30			result.Error = "host evidence unavailable"
31			if errors.Is(err, connection.ErrPythonUnavailable) {
32				result.Error = err.Error()
33			}
34			result.Capabilities = append(result.Capabilities, Capability{Name: "python3", Available: false, Detail: result.Error})
35			return result, err
36		}
37		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &result); err != nil || result.Protocol != 1 {
38			return result, errors.New("host helper returned an unsupported evidence format")
39		}
40		result.Scope = scope
41		result.Capabilities = append(result.Capabilities, Capability{Name: "python3", Available: true})
42		for i := range result.Requests {

189		type answer struct {
190			value string
191			err   error
192		}
193		ch := make(chan answer, 1)
194		go func() {
195			line, err := bufio.NewReader(io.LimitReader(in, 1024)).ReadString('\n')
196			ch <- answer{line, err}
197		}()
198		select {
199		case <-ctx.Done():
200			return false, ctx.Err()
201		case a := <-ch:
202			if a.err != nil && a.err != io.EOF {
203				return false, a.err
204			}
205			value := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(a.value))
206			return value == "y" || value == "yes", nil
207		}
208	}

25	func digest(v any) string {
26		raw, _ := json.Marshal(v)
27		sum := sha256.Sum256(raw)
28		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])

30	func call(ctx context.Context, t config.Target, r Request, o Options) (Status, error) {
31		if o.Host != nil {
32			return o.Host(ctx, t, r)
33		}
34		raw, _ := json.Marshal(r)
35		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 90*time.Second)
36		defer cancel()
37		out, err := connection.ExecutePython(ctx, t.SSHHost, hostScript, raw, 1<<20)
38		if err != nil {
39			return Status{}, err
40		}
41		var s Status
42		if json.Unmarshal(out, &s) != nil {
43			return s, errors.New("invalid client service response")
44		}
45		if s.Error != "" {
46			return s, errors.New(s.Error)
47		}
48		return s, nil
49	}
50	func validTarget(t config.Target) error {
51		if t.Transient || t.TransportOverride || t.ID == "" {
52			return errors.New("existing service operations require a saved target endpoint and SSH host")
53		}
54		if t.ManagedCoreID != "" {
55			return errors.New("this target has a managed installation; use cores lifecycle commands")
56		}
57		return nil
58	}
59	func Inspect(ctx context.Context, t config.Target, o Options) (Status, error) {
60		if err := validTarget(t); err != nil {
61			return Status{}, err
62		}
63		if t.Service == nil {
64			return Status{}, errors.New("bind the existing service with targets service bind first")
65		}
66		if err := config.ValidateClientService(t.Service); err != nil {
67			return Status{}, err
68		}
69		return call(ctx, t, Request{Op: "status", Service: *t.Service}, o)
70	}

73	func PrepareBind(ctx context.Context, t config.Target, candidate config.ClientService, o Options) (Plan, error) {
74		if err := validTarget(t); err != nil {
75			return Plan{}, err
76		}
77		if candidate.Kind == "docker" && !config.ValidDockerHost(candidate.DockerHost) {

84		if err = config.ValidateClientService(&s.Binding); err != nil {
85			return Plan{}, err

88		p.Digest = planDigest(t, p)
89		return p, nil

29	func execute(ctx context.Context, args []string, in io.Reader, out, errOut io.Writer, deps Dependencies) int {
30		cmd := New(deps)
31		cmd.SetArgs(append([]string{}, args...))
32		cmd.SetIn(in)
33		cmd.SetOut(out)
34		cmd.SetErr(errOut)
35		jsonMode := jsonRequested(cmd, args)
36		if err := cmd.ExecuteContext(ctx); err != nil {
37			if jsonMode {
38				encoder := json.NewEncoder(errOut)
39				encoder.SetEscapeHTML(false)
40				_ = encoder.Encode(errorEnvelope{Error: describeError(err)})
41			} else {
42				_, _ = fmt.Fprintln(errOut, "lazyclash:", core.Sanitize(err.Error()))
43			}
44			return ExitCode(err)
45		}
46		return 0
47	}

17	var shaPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`)
18	var versionPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[v]?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(?:[-.][A-Za-z0-9]+)*$`)
19	
20	const DefaultXrayVersion = "v26.10.29"
21	const DefaultHysteriaVersion = "app/v2.13.0"
22	
23	// resolveArtifact resolves immutable upstream artifacts at review time. GitHub
24	// asset digests and OCI manifests are pinned before any remote mutation.
25	func resolveArtifact(ctx context.Context, r Request, arch string) (Artifact, error) {
26		if arch != "amd64" && arch != "arm64" {
27			return Artifact{}, errors.New("server architecture must be amd64 or arm64")
28		}
29		repo, tag, asset := "XTLS/Xray-core", r.Version, "Xray-linux-64.zip"
30		if tag == "" {
31			tag = DefaultXrayVersion
32			if r.Recipe == "hysteria2" {
33				tag = DefaultHysteriaVersion
34			}
35		}
36		if arch == "arm64" {
37			asset = "Xray-linux-arm64-v8a.zip"
38		}
39		if r.Recipe == "hysteria2" {
40			repo, asset = "HyNetworks/hysteria", "hysteria-linux-"+arch
41			if tag != "" && tag != "latest" {
42				tag = "app/v" + strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimPrefix(tag, "app/"), "v")
43			}
44		} else if tag != "" && tag != "latest" {
45			tag = "v" + strings.TrimPrefix(tag, "v")
46		}
47		endpoint := "https://api.github.com/repos/" + repo + "/releases/latest"
48		if tag != "" && tag != "latest" {
49			endpoint = "https://api.github.com/repos/" + repo + "/releases/tags/" + url.PathEscape(tag)
50		}
51		var release struct {
52			Tag    string `json:"tag_name"`
53			Assets []struct {
54				Name   string `json:"name"`
55				URL    string `json:"browser_download_url"`
56				Digest string `json:"digest"`
57			} `json:"assets"`
58		}
59		body, _, err := getArtifact(ctx, endpoint, nil, 4<<20)
60		if err != nil {
61			return Artifact{}, errors.New("cannot resolve the official release; retry or specify a published version")
62		}
63		if json.Unmarshal(body, &release) != nil || release.Tag == "" || (tag != "latest" && release.Tag != tag) {
64			return Artifact{}, errors.New("official release response is invalid")
65		}
66		a := Artifact{Version: release.Tag, Arch: arch, Source: endpoint}
67		for _, v := range release.Assets {
68			if v.Name == asset {
69				a.URL, a.SHA256 = v.URL, strings.TrimPrefix(v.Digest, "sha256:")
70				break
71			}
72		}
73		if !shaPattern.MatchString(a.SHA256) || !strings.HasPrefix(a.URL, "https://github.com/"+repo+"/releases/download/") {
74			return Artifact{}, errors.New("official release is missing a SHA256-pinned architecture asset")
75		}
76		if r.Recipe == "hysteria2" {
77			// The project's official download service serves versioned binaries;
78			// verify against the same GitHub release digest at installation time.
79			a.URL = "https://download.hysteria.network/" + a.Version + "/" + asset
80		}
81		if r.Backend == "compose" {
82			registry, imageRepo, tag := "ghcr.io", "xtls/xray-core", strings.TrimPrefix(a.Version, "v")
83			if r.Recipe == "hysteria2" {
84				registry, imageRepo, tag = "registry-1.docker.io", "tobyxdd/hysteria", strings.TrimPrefix(a.Version, "app/")
85			}
86			a.Image, err = resolveImage(ctx, registry, imageRepo, tag)
87			if err != nil {
88				return Artifact{}, err
89			}
90			if r.Recipe == "legacy-vmess-ws-tls" {
91				a.NginxImage, err = resolveImage(ctx, "registry-1.docker.io", "library/nginx", "stable-alpine")
92				if err != nil {
93					return Artifact{}, err
94				}
95			}
96		}
97		return a, nil
98	}
99	
100	func resolveImage(ctx context.Context, registry, repo, tag string) (string, error) {
101		authURL := "https://ghcr.io/token?service=ghcr.io&scope=" + url.QueryEscape("repository:"+repo+":pull")
102		if registry == "registry-1.docker.io" {
103			authURL = "https://auth.docker.io/token?service=registry.docker.io&scope=" + url.QueryEscape("repository:"+repo+":pull")
104		}
105		body, _, err := getArtifact(ctx, authURL, nil, 1<<20)
106		if err != nil {
107			return "", errors.New("cannot obtain public registry download token")
108		}
109		var token struct {
110			Token string `json:"token"`
111		}
112		if json.Unmarshal(body, &token) != nil || token.Token == "" {
113			return "", errors.New("invalid registry response")
114		}
115		headers := map[string]string{"Authorization": "Bearer " + token.Token, "Accept": "application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json, application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json, application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json, application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json"}
116		body, h, err := getArtifact(ctx, "https://"+registry+"/v2/"+repo+"/manifests/"+url.PathEscape(tag), headers, 4<<20)
117		if err != nil {
118			return "", errors.New("cannot resolve the official container image tag to an immutable digest")
119		}
120		digest := strings.TrimPrefix(h.Get("Docker-Content-Digest"), "sha256:")
121		sum := sha256.Sum256(body)
122		if !shaPattern.MatchString(digest) || digest != hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]) {
123			return "", errors.New("container manifest digest verification failed")
124		}
125		if registry == "registry-1.docker.io" {
126			registry = "docker.io"
127		}
128		return registry + "/" + repo + "@sha256:" + digest, nil
129	}
130	
131	func getArtifact(ctx context.Context, address string, headers map[string]string, limit int64) ([]byte, http.Header, error) {
132		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 45*time.Second)
133		defer cancel()
134		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, address, nil)
135		if err != nil {
136			return nil, nil, err
137		}
138		req.Header.Set("User-Agent", "lazyclash-serverdeploy")
139		for k, v := range headers {
140			req.Header.Set(k, v)
141		}
142		resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
143		if err != nil {
144			return nil, nil, err
145		}
146		defer resp.Body.Close()
147		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
148			return nil, nil, errors.New("upstream request failed")
149		}
150		data, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, limit+1))
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, nil, err
153		}
154		if int64(len(data)) > limit {
155			return nil, nil, errors.New("upstream response exceeds limit")
156		}
157		return data, resp.Header, nil

````text
1	# 安裝與管理 Mihomo client
2	
3	`setup` 建立一個 lazyclash-owned client，記錄 binary／image 版本、服務、設定來源與
4	target。既有 Verge、其他 system service 和未知容器仍由原 owner 管理。
5	
6	```sh
7	lazyclash setup
8	lazyclash cores list --json
9	lazyclash cores status workstation --json
10	lazyclash cores configure workstation --interactive
11	```
12	
13	Wizard 可選本機或 SSH、native 或 Docker，匯入 share links、節點訂閱或完整 YAML，
14	配置群組／starter、TUN 與 system proxy，最後檢查具體變更再套用。只提供部分 business
15	參數時不自動進 wizard；使用 `--interactive` 明確補齊。JSON 模式不提示 sudo／SSH 密碼。
16	
17	## 可重現的 CLI 流程
18	
19	```sh
20	lazyclash --ssh home-server setup home-core --backend native \
21	  --input-kind links --input /absolute/private/nodes.txt --preset cn-split --json
22	
23	# 檢查上一步的版本、端口、來源、權限、blockers 和 digest 後：
24	lazyclash --ssh home-server setup home-core --backend native \
25	  --input-kind links --input /absolute/private/nodes.txt --preset cn-split \
26	  --yes --expect REVIEWED_DIGEST
27	```
28	
29	Native 使用固定官方版本與 asset SHA-256；Docker 固定官方 image digest，要求已有可用
30	daemon／Compose，不隱式安裝 Docker。預設使用 loopback controller／mixed port、
31	生成 API [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]，遇到端口衝突要求更換，不停掉原有服務。
32	
33	Proxy 模式使用 user service；需要 TUN 時使用 system scope 和 root-owned 檔案。
34	`--boot` 控制可用 host policy 下的 boot/login 自啟；Linux user service 不自動開啟 linger。
35	系統權限交給原生 sudo／SSH，TUI 本身維持一般使用者權限。
36	
37	Docker bridge 模式在 container 內監聽對應端口、只發佈到 host loopback；其 container
38	listener 不能直接當成外部 host endpoint。Host TUN 支援矩陣與 VPN 檢查見
39	[VPN 共存](vpn-coexistence.md)。
40	
41	成功後自動加入 targets，分別回報 service、API 與 proxy request 狀態。Proxy request
42	失敗不等於安裝不存在；保留 receipt 與私人資料，先看 `cores status` 再決定下一步。
43	Configure 保留核心版本、backend、service scope／身份及 listener ports；遷移這些
44	邊界使用另一個明確規劃的 instance。
45	
46	## Starter、地區分流與 GitHub 不可達
47	
48	```sh
49	lazyclash rules preset list --json
50	lazyclash --target home-core rules preset apply cn-split --json
51	lazyclash --target home-core rules preset update --json
52	```
53	
54	`cn-split`：本機／VPN bypass、reject／direct／proxy 明確分類、CN domain／IP 直連，
55	其餘交給 PROXY。可選 AI、Apple、媒體分類並明確映射到 policy；不從節點名稱猜地區。
56	`simple`：本機／VPN bypass，其餘 PROXY。完整 YAML 預設 `preserve`，避免默默替換使用者規則。
57	
58	這些規則資料隨 binary 附帶，使用本地 providers，不需要首次從 GitHub 下載 geodata。
59	來源是 clash-rules 的 immutable `rules-<SHA-256>` artifact，逐檔驗 hash，保留原始
60	manifest、lock 與授權。手工規則與 mirrored geo data 的授權分開標示。
61	`preset update` 使用目前 lazyclash binary 所附的快照；啟動不會浮動更新規則。
62	
63	Core binary／image 和節點本身仍需可取得。可選已存在 target 作為明確 bootstrap data
64	proxy，或使用已驗證的本地 artifact／image archive；不能依賴尚未啟動的新 core 下載
65	它自己需要的檔案。下載失敗保留草稿／舊資料，不切換到隱含環境代理。
66	
67	訂閱是 node provider，初始可用快照納入私人設定；完整 YAML 另走匯入路徑並檢查
68	provider、檔案與 geodata 依賴。這裡的「離線 starter」是規則建立不用連 GitHub，
69	不代表無網路也能存取代理出口。
70	
71	參考 [clash-rules 發佈契約](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/clash-rules/blob/main/docs/release-pipeline.md)
72	與 [第三方資料說明](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/clash-rules/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY.md)。
73	Docker 範例參考 [DockerCompose-V2Ray 的 client 子目錄](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/DockerCompose-V2Ray/tree/9e6f3b957edbbaf2bbcfd9deea8d871873069e56/clients/mihomo-docker)，
74	不執行其 Xray server／防火牆部署。
75	
76	## 停止與移除
77	
78	```sh
79	lazyclash cores stop home-core --json
80	lazyclash cores stop home-core --yes --expect REVIEWED_DIGEST
81	lazyclash cores remove home-core --json
82	```
83	
84	Start／stop／restart／remove 都先預覽再套用。只有已記錄且重新核對的 owner 可操作；
85	remove 預設保留私人設定、備份與操作紀錄。System proxy 還原遇到使用者後續改動時回報
86	衝突，不強制蓋回舊設定。未 ACK 的新 TUN 會被 rollback 並避免於下一次 boot 自動復活。
87
````

Importing the node is a separate reviewed operation that may reload the bound client; it does not explicitly select HY2, but adding it to an automatic group can change traffic. ## Gaps relevant to a local doctor

1. **No combined, URL-free health report.** Existing commands expose separate layers; none reconciles settings, API, resolved data endpoint, environment, OS proxy and service state.
2. **Failure can hide useful evidence.** `proxy status` collects environment/OS information, then returns before printing if resolution fails: `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/lazyclash/internal/cli/proxy_env.go:176–191`. Malformed settings similarly stop most target-oriented commands.
3. **No unified consistency findings.** The pieces do not comprehensively identify stale env/OS endpoints versus the selected runtime listeners. Configured ports are not proof of listening or successful forwarding.
4. **Unknowns are unevenly represented.** `SystemProxy` returns an empty map on unsupported platforms or command failure; a doctor should distinguish unavailable from disabled.
5. **Network findings are setup-oriented.** An already enabled core TUN is labeled a conflict because it warns against adding another TUN—not because the existing proxy is broken: `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/lazyclash/internal/networkcheck/inspect.go:216–217`.
6. **Controller and data-path resolution differ.** Proxy commands can infer local runtime ports, whereas URL/IP/latency diagnostics expect an explicitly registered data proxy. API failure must not imply the data proxy is unusable.

## Conclusion

**The repository already supports the requested workflow without new deployment code:** Azure VM creation through the official `az` CLI → native Hysteria 2 deployment over SSH → isolated proxy verification → separately reviewed local-client import.

The key unresolved inputs are:

- Which **Hanru Azure login, tenant and enabled subscription** to use.
- Hong Kong region/SKU availability and current price. **`eastasia` is the intended Azure region to verify**, not a repository-pinned region.
- An existing SSH public key, usable corresponding private key, and administrator IPv4 CIDR.
- A **public DNS hostname for HY2’s trusted certificate**.
- The intended local client target, source owner, destination group, and whether actually switching traffic is authorized.

I inspected repository files only. No Azure/SSH access, provisioning, local configuration inspection outside the repository, tests, or proxy changes were performed.

## Minimum viable deployment

| Item | Repository requirement / recommendation |
|---|---|
| OS | **Ubuntu 24.04 LTS**, strictly enforced by deployment preflight |
| Architecture | Linux **amd64 or arm64** |
| CPU / memory | Azure picker enforces **≥1 vCPU and ≥1 GiB RAM**; docs call 1 vCPU/1 GB a starting point, not a throughput guarantee |
| Azure disk | **32 GiB Standard SSD LRS** minimum and default; smaller disks are rejected |
| Backend | **Native systemd**, default; avoids Docker overhead/dependencies |
| Server | Pinned **Hysteria `app/v2.13.0`** |
| Verification client | Existing compatible Mihomo preferred; otherwise verified download, currently **v1.19.33** |
| Privileges | SSH as `ubuntu` for managed Azure creation; remote Python 3 and root/noninteractive sudo for the fixed Python helper |
| Networking | Standard static public IPv4; working DNS, outbound downloads/ACME and inbound UDP |
| TLS | Public DNS hostname + Let’s Encrypt HTTP challenge; TCP 80 must remain reachable for renewal |

Automatic Azure selection considers only these recommended SKUs:

- `Standard_B1s`
- `Standard_B2ats_v2`
- `Standard_B2pts_v2`
- `Standard_B2ts_v2`

It chooses the lowest **fully priced compatible total fixed cost** among those available, rather than exhaustively finding Azure’s cheapest VM. An explicit `--plan` can select another compatible SKU. `--architecture auto` permits both ARM and x86.

Prices include compute, root disk and static IPv4; outbound traffic, disk transactions and tax are additional. B-series burst-credit exhaustion can reduce sustained throughput. **Do not use the documented US-region ~$12.18/month snapshot as a Hong Kong quote.**

### 3. Establish SSH and DNS, then deploy HY2

Cloud creation uploads **only the public key**; it does not automatically configure the corresponding local private-key identity. Managed Azure hosts are recorded as `ubuntu@PUBLIC_IP`. Ensure that identity is usable through existing OpenSSH configuration/default keys/agent, and verify the server host key before unattended use.

Deployment preflight already performs the authoritative remote inspection:

```sh
lazyclash servers deploy hy2-hk --host azure-hk \
  --recipe hysteria2 --backend native \
  --public-host "$PUBLIC_IPV4" --domain "$HY2_DOMAIN" \
  --email "$ACME_EMAIL" --obfs none --json

After review, repeat with:

```sh
--yes --expect "$REVIEWED_SERVER_DIGEST"
```

`--email` is optional; omission explicitly uses Certbot’s no-email registration. `--obfs salamander` is supported but is not necessary for the minimum baseline. It generates a separate persistent obfuscation [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], removes standard HTTP/3 masquerade compatibility and does not bypass blanket UDP blocking.

Then inspect the returned result and:

lazyclash servers status hy2-hk --json
```

Require an authenticated verification result, not merely a running systemd service.

## SSH, TLS and ports

### SSH/preflight behavior

The fixed helper checks:

- Ubuntu release, CPU architecture and `systemctl`.
- Deployment directory, ownership manifest, existing unit/Compose project conflicts.
- IPv4 and, where available, IPv6 bind availability for required ports.
- Certificate-domain resolution and overlap with the public endpoint’s resolved addresses.
- Existing certificate-name conflicts.
- Docker/Compose availability for BYO Compose hosts.
- Active UFW, reported as a warning—not automatically repaired.

Background SSH uses `BatchMode=yes`, `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes`, an eight-second connect timeout, and preserves existing OpenSSH alias/key/jump-host configuration. It elevates using `sudo -n python3 -c <fixed helper>`; request data stays on stdin.

There is **no remote CPU/RAM minimum measurement** in server preflight: sizing checks are in the Azure picker.

- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/lazyclash/internal/serverdeploy/service.go:28`

### TLS/hostname/IP choices

- `--public-host` accepts an IP or DNS hostname; clients use it as the connection address.
- `--domain` must be a DNS hostname and becomes HY2 client `sni`.
- Thus **connect-to-IP + certificate/SNI hostname is supported**.
- IP-only certificates, custom certificate paths, self-signed deployment and skip-verification switches are **not exposed by the shipped server recipe**.
- Azure provisioning does **not** assign a public-IP DNS label or create DNS records. A separately configured provider hostname could be evaluated, but it is not automated/tested here.
- DNS preflight checks address overlap, **not proof that public ACME validation can reach this VM**. TCP 80 and correct public A/AAAA routing remain operational requirements.

### Actual exposure and installed services

| Port/service | Behavior |
|---|---|
| TCP 22 | SSH; **default CIDR is `0.0.0.0/0`**, so explicitly supply the administrator `/32` or intended IPv4 CIDR |
| UDP 443 | Default HY2 listener, public |
| TCP 80 | Certbot standalone challenge/renewal; public reachability must remain available |
| TCP 443 | Azure’s generic NSG also opens this, although HY2 does not need a TCP listener |
| Local probe | Random authenticated loopback mixed port; no live controller/TUN change |

Installed native service:

- Unit: `lazyclash-server-hy2-hk.service`
- Configuration: `/var/lib/lazyclash/servers/hy2-hk/config.yaml`
- Executable: `/var/lib/lazyclash/servers/hy2-hk/bin/hysteria`
- Invocation: `hysteria server --config …`
- Certificate directory: `/etc/letsencrypt/live/lazyclash-hy2-hk/`
- Renewal: `certbot.timer`, with an owned deploy hook that restarts the running service.

The unit runs as root with systemd filesystem restrictions, `NoNewPrivileges` and capabilities limited to `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE`.

Custom ports require separate firewall work. Managed deployments currently reject another service with the same numerical listen port **even when one is TCP and one UDP**.

## Local client: import versus activation

### Safest existing-client workflow

First identify the actual target and binding:

```sh
lazyclash targets list --json
lazyclash --target "$TARGET" status --json
lazyclash --target "$TARGET" configs source show --json
lazyclash --target "$TARGET" proxies list --json
```

A controller-only target is insufficient for persistent edits. It needs an explicit native/Docker/Verge configuration-source binding.

To keep the node out of an existing automatic group initially:

```sh
lazyclash --target "$TARGET" servers connect hy2-hk \
  --create-group HY2-Test --json
```

After reviewing the source diff:

```sh
lazyclash --target "$TARGET" servers connect hy2-hk \
  --create-group HY2-Test --yes --expect "$REVIEWED_CLIENT_DIGEST" --json
```

A new group does not modify parent-group membership or routing rules. Alternatively use `--group "$GROUP"` with an actual existing group name.

**Does this change the active proxy?**

- Server deployment/probing: **no live-client change**.
- Export: **no activation**.
- `servers connect`: modifies the bound source and can activate/reload it:
  - Native: controller configuration reload.
  - Docker: reload; single-file mounts may require an owned container restart.
  - Unowned Verge: `persisted_pending_owner_reload`; reactivate the profile in Verge, then verify.
  - Lazyclash-owned Verge: native-owner activation can happen automatically.
- Import **does not issue an explicit proxy-selection operation**. However, automatic groups, filters, reload behavior or owner regeneration can affect traffic. Do not promise an entirely traffic-neutral import.

After activation:

```sh
lazyclash --target "$TARGET" servers connect hy2-hk --verify --json
lazyclash --target "$TARGET" proxies delay hy2-hk --json
```

An intentional active-group switch is separate and immediate:

```sh
lazyclash --target "$TARGET" proxies select "$GROUP" hy2-hk --json
```

Use it only if the group contains that node and switching is authorized; preserve the previous selection for restoration.

lazyclash servers export hy2-hk --format mihomo --output "$[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]_NODE_FILE"
lazyclash servers export hy2-hk --format starter --output "$[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]_STARTER_FILE"

## Safety and implementation caveats

1. **Failed proxy verification can still exit successfully.** The deployment returns `installed-unverified` with warnings when the probe fails. Check result status, verification time and observed exit IP. `servers status` observes current service state but reports the *last* full proxy verification.  
   `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/lazyclash/internal/serverdeploy/service.go:295`

2. The verifier uses a private temporary Mihomo, authenticated loopback proxy and real HTTPS requests to IP.SB/Cloudflare. Endpoint redundancy never falls back to DIRECT. `--verify-interface NAME` changes only that verifier’s interface selection.  
   `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/lazyclash/internal/serverprobe/probe.go:61`

3. Keep VM, deployment and client-import approvals separate. Identity/artifact/source changes invalidate reviewed plans. Preserve journals and use status/resume/verify after uncertain writes rather than creating duplicates.

4. Stop is not cleanup: Azure stop deallocates compute but retains disk/IP charges. Remove the managed server before reviewed VM deletion. Cleanup only deletes resources with proven ownership.

5. The offline guide defaults its server example to **VLESS**, so substitute the HY2 command above. Its Azure raw-command renderer also puts subscription flags before command names, unlike the corrected adapter. Use the command-first `az account … --subscription …` examples above.  
   `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/lazyclash/internal/cli/vps_guide.go:182`

# Go CLI / TUI

Build around **see → select → act → see the result**. Keep context visible,
common actions discoverable, and navigation responsive while work runs. These
are opinionated defaults for new tools and features; respect existing contracts.

## Boundaries and defaults

- Use for Go commands, dashboards, pickers, wizards, and interaction fixes.
  A one-shot picker need not become a full-screen dashboard.
- Prefer Cobra for a command tree; Bubble Tea, Bubbles, and Lip Gloss for TUI;
  Huh when a form earns its complexity. A tiny CLI can use `flag`. Retain a
  working framework in an existing project.
- Read `go.mod` before examples. For greenfield work, choose compatible stable
  Charm versions, verify Go requirements, and pin `go.mod`/`go.sum`.
- Lazygit's implementation is an in-tree gocui fork, not Bubble Tea. Borrow
  interaction principles without copying its Git actions, layout, or every key.
- This is a development skill, not a Lazygit usage guide or general Go tutorial.
  Release-channel work can use the optional
  [cli-release-distribution guide](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/cli-release-distribution).
  No other skill is required to use this package.

## Workflow

- [ ] **1. Ground the task.** Read the command tree, services, config, terminal
  setup, and tests. Identify the repeated task, necessary state, target OSes,
  and whether it needs a command, picker, wizard, or dashboard. For a distributed
  CLI, include its installation and upgrade paths in the interaction scope. Infer from the
  repo; ask only about consequential product choices that remain unknown.
- [ ] **2. Define the interaction.** Sketch the primary screen and one complete
  action path using the compact contract below. Record focus, keyboard behavior,
  entry conditions, and failure/cancel behavior before wiring widgets.
- [ ] **3. Build a vertical slice.** Connect a real operation from CLI and UI to
  the same domain service, validation, and result. Keep handlers and views thin;
  add packages as responsibilities grow, rather than generating empty layers.
- [ ] **4. Complete the states.** Handle loading, successful empty results,
  errors, refresh, cancellation, resize, and return from overlays or external
  programs. Add configuration for actual recurring preferences.
- [ ] **5. Verify and finish.** Run relevant checks, fix failures, and exercise
  the interaction in a PTY. Report changes, evidence, and untested paths.
  For a published CLI, verify how an existing installation reaches the next
  version; a successful fresh install alone does not cover that journey.
  Complete an authorized build request; do not stop after producing a design.

### Compact interaction contract

Use in working notes or the implementation explanation. Do not require a new
specification file for a small change; omit inapplicable rows.

```text
Task:           repeated action and state needed to decide
Surface:        command / inline picker / wizard / dashboard
Layout:         list, detail/preview, status; narrow-screen behavior
Navigation:     focus, arrows + Vim aliases, search, Back, help
Entry:          bare command, flags, --interactive, non-TTY/JSON
Operation:      shared service, validation, target, result, cancellation
State:          selection identity, async ownership, freshness, failure
Configuration:  preferences, paths, precedence, effective-config view
Acceptance:     input sequence and observable expected result
```

## Interaction invariants

1. **Stable context.** Keep pane roles, per-view selection, scroll, and filter.
   Refresh follows identity, not an old row number. Show focus separately from
   selection and status colors.
2. **Two navigation vocabularies.** Support arrows and `j/k`, Tab/Shift+Tab for
   focus, and context-appropriate `h/l`. Add `gg/G` for long lists. No required
   normal/insert mode. Advertise only applicable actions.
3. **Typing owns printable keys.** Route events through the modal and focused
   widget before navigation shortcuts. Typing `j`, `q`, `/`, or an action's
   mnemonic in a field must not invoke that action.
4. **Discoverable speed.** Provide a short contextual footer, `?` help, and an
   action menu when needed. Derive hints and dispatch from the same effective
   bindings and availability definitions.
5. **Immediate feedback.** Render available state before slow discovery; allow
   navigation during I/O. Show pending, success, and failure while retaining
   useful rows. Avoid decorative motion that competes with the task.
6. **Proportional confirmation.** Destructive actions name the exact target and
   consequence. Reversible navigation stays immediate. A mutating wizard ends
   with one meaningful review/submit step.

Read [interaction-design.md](references/interaction-design.md) when laying out
screens or implementing navigation, filtering, help, mouse behavior, or resize.

## CLI and wizard entry policy

Parse flags and validate syntax before deciding whether to prompt. Interactive
behavior follows intent, not merely the existence of a terminal.

| Invocation | Default |
|---|---|
| Bare app with a dashboard, interactive terminal | Open dashboard |
| Bare command explicitly designated wizard-capable, e.g. `create` | Open wizard |
| Bare ordinary command group | Show help |
| Partial business flags/arguments, required data missing | Usage error, example, help hint |
| Complete valid business flags/arguments | Execute command path |
| Explicit `--interactive` | Prefill from flags/config; collect remaining choices |
| Non-TTY or machine-output mode | Never prompt; produce data, help, or clear error |
| Invalid flag/value, even with `--interactive` | Report error; do not turn a typo into a wizard |

Global options such as `--config` and `--color` do not alone signal business
command intent. An explicit UI request without a usable TTY or combined with
JSON output is an error. Make equivalent operations scriptable; keep stdout
clean and diagnostics separate.

Read [cli-wizards-config.md](references/cli-wizards-config.md) for commands,
guided setup, validation, configuration, or shell integration.

## Implementation and verification references

- Read [charm-stack.md](references/charm-stack.md) when selecting dependencies,
  finding an existing component, or adapting version-sensitive examples. It maps
  needs to official libraries/tools; it is not a bulk-install instruction.
- Read [async-terminal.md](references/async-terminal.md) for background work,
  startup performance, or terminal handoffs. It includes dev-cli lessons with
  sources and performance evidence guidance.
- Read [agent-facing-cli.md](references/agent-facing-cli.md) when a tool needs
  an embedded operational skill or a dependable automation interface. Keep
  agent and human entry points on the same services; a bundled skill is optional.
- Read [go-distribution.md](references/go-distribution.md) when preparing a Go
  CLI for other users: start with the actual main-package install path, version
  reporting, published tags, and separate source/module packaging boundaries;
  add package managers when the release needs them.
- Read [shell-completion.md](references/shell-completion.md) for native generators,
  user install/status, fpath activation, offline candidates and real shell tests.
- Read [shell-context.md](references/shell-context.md) when exporting a parent-shell
  environment, owning persistent connections, or generating consumer configuration.
- Read [self-update.md](references/self-update.md) when making a CLI installable,
  preparing its first release, or adding an upgrade command.
  Choose source, release assets, or the owning package manager from evidence;
  verify the effective installed copy while preserving local builds by default.
- Read [verification.md](references/verification.md) before declaring an
  interaction implemented. Select applicable cases, use deterministic state
  tests, and exercise a real PTY; screenshots cannot prove input behavior.

## Installed-tool lifecycle

For a CLI with supported, versioned user installations, provide a discoverable
`upgrade` entry point and a read-only `upgrade --check` by default. Follow an
established equivalent command name when the project already has one. If the
product deliberately omits this entry point, record the reason and its supported
external upgrade path; do not leave it out simply because the task focused on
the dashboard. Experimental one-off programs need no release machinery.

An explicit upgrade should execute the supported owning package manager under
the CLI's normal confirmation policy. A recognized, supported Homebrew install
should not stop at printing `brew upgrade`. Keep manual guidance for unsupported
or ambiguous ownership. A small manager adapter is enough; this default does not
require adding a standalone downloader or compiler. When a manager requires the
running program to exit, expose an observable handoff and a final-result query;
accepted work is not completed work. Updating the CLI must remain
separate from updating its managed service, data, or configuration.

## Gotchas

- **Charm v1/v2 examples are not interchangeable.** Bubble Tea v2 uses
  `charm.land/bubbletea/v2`, `tea.KeyPressMsg`, and `View() tea.View`; v1 uses
  the older module, `tea.KeyMsg`, and `View() string`. Huh/Bubbles must match
  the model generation. A UX fix is not permission to migrate the app.
- **Async wrappers can still freeze startup.** Blocking constructors, config
  probes, first-frame work, or synchronous `Update`/`View` work block input.
  Move the actual slow work into effects.
- **Late results remain late after cancellation.** Correlate results with the
  current request before changing state. Cancelled waiting also does not prove
  a remote write was rolled back.
- **Bytes/runes are not terminal widths.** Use ANSI-aware cell measurement and
  grapheme-safe truncation; test Chinese, combining marks, and emoji. Clamp
  sizes after subtracting actual borders/padding, including tiny resizes.
- **A character device is not necessarily a TTY.** Detect the actual input and
  output terminals. Machine-output intent suppresses UI even with a TTY.
- **A flag default is not an explicit override.** Preserve changed-flag
  information for explicit `false`, `0`, and empty values. Cobra validation
  hooks can run before `RunE`; check ordering before expecting a wizard to fill
  a required flag.
- **`os.UserConfigDir()` does not enforce XDG everywhere.** macOS uses
  Application Support. Implement the chosen XDG policy explicitly; persistent
  state belongs outside both disposable cache and the preferences file.
- **Nested terminal readers compete.** Integrate a form into the current model
  or release/suspend the outer program before running another reader. Restore
  terminal modes before children/editors and on handled exit paths.

This package contains instructions and references, not a generator or starter.
Preferences are original synthesis; project observations and official contracts
are identified in the references.

23	// Execute is the process boundary: stdout belongs to command data; errors are
24	// rendered exactly once on stderr after command resources have been released.
25	func Execute(ctx context.Context, args []string, in io.Reader, out, errOut io.Writer) int {
26		return execute(ctx, args, in, out, errOut, Dependencies{})
27	}
28	
29	func execute(ctx context.Context, args []string, in io.Reader, out, errOut io.Writer, deps Dependencies) int {
30		cmd := New(deps)
31		cmd.SetArgs(append([]string{}, args...))
32		cmd.SetIn(in)
33		cmd.SetOut(out)
34		cmd.SetErr(errOut)
35		jsonMode := jsonRequested(cmd, args)
36		if err := cmd.ExecuteContext(ctx); err != nil {
37			if jsonMode {
38				encoder := json.NewEncoder(errOut)
39				encoder.SetEscapeHTML(false)
40				_ = encoder.Encode(errorEnvelope{Error: describeError(err)})
41			} else {
42				_, _ = fmt.Fprintln(errOut, "lazyclash:", core.Sanitize(err.Error()))
43			}
44			return ExitCode(err)
45		}
46		return 0
47	}
48	
49	type errorEnvelope struct {
50		Error errorDetails `json:"error"`
51	}
52	
53	type errorDetails struct {
54		Code       string `json:"code"`
55		Message    string `json:"message"`
56		Operation  string `json:"operation,omitempty"`
57		HTTPStatus int    `json:"http_status,omitempty"`
58	}
59	
60	func describeError(err error) errorDetails {
61		result := errorDetails{Code: "runtime", Message: core.Sanitize(err.Error())}
62		var controllerErr *core.Error
63		var usageErr *UsageError
64		var proxyAmbiguous *proxyenv.AmbiguousError
65		var authorization *tailnet.AuthorizationRequiredError
66		switch {
67		case errors.As(err, &controllerErr):
68			// Preserve unknown-write-result even when its cause is cancellation.
69			result.Code = string(controllerErr.Kind)
70			result.Operation = controllerErr.Operation
71			result.HTTPStatus = controllerErr.StatusCode
72		case errors.As(err, &usageErr), strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "unknown command "):
73			result.Code = "usage"
74		case errors.As(err, &authorization):
75			result.Code = "authorization-required"
76		case connection.IsAuthRequired(err):
77			result.Code = "ssh-auth-required"
78		case errors.As(err, &proxyAmbiguous):
79			result.Code = "proxy-target-ambiguous"
80		case errors.Is(err, proxyenv.ErrNoProxyConfigured):
81			result.Code = "proxy-not-configured"
82		case errors.Is(err, proxyenv.ErrTemporaryProxy):
83			result.Code = "proxy-temporary"
84		case errors.Is(err, config.ErrConflict), errors.Is(err, serverstate.ErrConflict):
85			result.Code = "config-conflict"
86		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled), errors.Is(err, wizard.ErrCanceled):
87			result.Code = "canceled"
88		case errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
89			result.Code = "timeout"
90		}
91		return result
92	}
93	
94	// Inspect output intent before execution so syntax errors can also be JSON.
95	// Respect flag values and the -- terminator instead of finding a substring in
96	// argv (a filename or filter value may itself be "--json"). Cobra remains the
97	// authority for syntax/argument validation.
98	func jsonRequested(root *cobra.Command, args []string) bool {
99		valueFlags := map[string]bool{}
100		var visit func(*cobra.Command)
101		visit = func(cmd *cobra.Command) {
102			for _, flags := range []*pflag.FlagSet{cmd.LocalNonPersistentFlags(), cmd.PersistentFlags()} {
103				flags.VisitAll(func(flag *pflag.Flag) {
104					if flag.NoOptDefVal == "" {
105						valueFlags["--"+flag.Name] = true
106						if flag.Shorthand != "" {
107							valueFlags["-"+flag.Shorthand] = true
108						}
109					}
110				})
111			}
112			for _, child := range cmd.Commands() {
113				visit(child)
114			}
115		}
116		visit(root)
117		requested := false
118		for i := 0; i < len(args); i++ {
119			arg := args[i]
120			if arg == "--" {
121				break
122			}
123			name, value, hasValue := strings.Cut(arg, "=")
124			if name == "--json" {
125				if !hasValue {
126					requested = true
127				} else if parsed, err := strconv.ParseBool(value); err == nil {
128					requested = parsed
129				}
130				continue
131			}
132			if !hasValue && valueFlags[name] {
133				i++
134			}
135		}
136		return requested
137	}
138

299		if !cmd.HasAvailableSubCommands() || cmd.Run != nil || cmd.RunE != nil {
300			return
301		}
302		cmd.Args = cobra.ArbitraryArgs
303		cmd.RunE = func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
304			if len(args) > 0 {
305				return unknownSubcommand(cmd, args[0])
306			}
307			if json, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("json"); json {
308				return usage("%s needs a subcommand for --json output; see --help", cmd.CommandPath())
309			}
310			return cmd.Help()
311		}
312	}
313	
314	func unknownSubcommand(cmd *cobra.Command, name string) error {
315		names := []string{}
316		for _, child := range cmd.Commands() {
317			if child.IsAvailableCommand() {
318				names = append(names, child.Name())
319			}
320		}
321		return usage("unknown %s subcommand %q; choose one of: %s", cmd.CommandPath(), name, strings.Join(names, ", "))
322	}
323	
324	func terminals(in io.Reader, out io.Writer) bool {
325		i, ok := in.(*os.File)
326		if !ok {
327			return false
328		}
329		o, ok := out.(*os.File)
330		return ok && term.IsTerminal(int(i.Fd())) && term.IsTerminal(int(o.Fd()))
331	}
332	
333	func argsExact(n int) cobra.PositionalArgs {
334		return func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
335			if n == 0 && len(args) > 0 && cmd.HasAvailableSubCommands() {
336				return unknownSubcommand(cmd, args[0])
337			}
338			if len(args) != n {
339				return usage("%s requires %d argument(s); see --help", cmd.CommandPath(), n)
340			}
341			return nil
342		}
343	}

````text
1	# CLI, wizards, and configuration
2	
3	Read when implementing commands, guided setup, preferences, or shell integration.
4	This contract is a default for new tools; preserve existing public behavior.
5	
6	## Contents
7	
8	- [Resolve invocation intent](#resolve-invocation-intent)
9	- [One operation, multiple entry points](#one-operation-multiple-entry-points)
10	- [Wizard experience](#wizard-experience)
11	- [Configuration](#configuration)
12	- [Sources](#sources)
13	
14	## Resolve invocation intent
15	
16	Declare which commands support a wizard. An ordinary noun group such as `hosts`
17	shows help; a designated `hosts add` can guide the user when called bare.
18	Do not infer a wizard for every missing argument.
19	
20	Resolve in this order:
21	
22	1. Parse syntax, unknown flags, invalid supplied values, and conflicting modes.
23	   `--help`/version remain usable without initializing a UI, network, or domain
24	   services. Config problems should not prevent access to basic help.
25	2. Check explicit output/interaction intent. `--json`, disabled input, or
26	   non-TTY execution suppress prompts. Explicit UI plus machine output or
27	   missing usable terminals is an error, not a silent fallback.
28	3. If `--interactive` is explicit, prefill a wizard with validated supplied
29	   values. If the designated command is bare in a TTY, enter its wizard.
30	4. Otherwise validate the operation as a command. Missing required data is a
31	   concise usage error naming the fields, one example, and the help command.
32	
33	Business arguments/flags express command intent, including explicit values
34	equal to defaults. Global presentation/config options alone do not. A bare
35	dashboard app opens its UI only in interactive mode. Without that capability,
36	bare roots/groups show help; a bare machine-output invocation without a data
37	operation reports a usage error instead of printing prose into JSON.
38	
39	```text
40	forgebox                             # dashboard, if one exists and TTY
41	forgebox hosts                       # command-group help
42	forgebox hosts add                   # designated wizard, TTY only
43	forgebox --config ./test.toml hosts add  # still a bare wizard entry
44	forgebox hosts add --name staging    # missing required address: usage error
45	forgebox hosts add --interactive --name staging  # prefilled wizard
46	forgebox hosts add --adress host     # unknown flag: error, never a wizard
47	```
48	
49	Inspect Cobra's hook order before implementing. Required-flag checks and `Args`
50	validation may execute before `RunE`. Do not mark a wizard-filled field required
51	unconditionally and expect the wizard to run. Separate supplied-value syntax
52	validation from completeness validation; both entry paths finish with the same
53	complete request validator. Root `PersistentPreRunE` is not a guarantee when a
54	child overrides the persistent hook; use an explicit shared initialization path
55	or the library's verified hook traversal contract.
56	
57	## One operation, multiple entry points
58	
59	Keep request construction, domain validation, execution, and presentation
60	separate. CLI flags, a standalone wizard, and a dashboard action all produce
61	the same typed request and call the same service. Tests can inject readers,
62	writers, services, and cancellation without launching a real terminal.
63	
64	- In Cobra, return errors from handlers and write through `OutOrStdout()` and
65	  `ErrOrStderr()`. Let the entrypoint choose an exit status after cleanup.
66	- Write command data to stdout; diagnostics to stderr. UI rendering must have
67	  exclusive ownership of its terminal stream. JSON contains no progress/ANSI.
68	- Default exit contract: success 0, runtime failure 1, usage/config error 2,
69	  interrupted/cancelled requested operation 130. Closing an idle dashboard is
70	  success. Preserve child status when the command's purpose is transparent
71	  execution. Document intentional variations.
72	- Where an operation requires confirmation, provide a documented noninteractive
73	  approval path; missing approval fails instead of waiting for input. Scale
74	  confirmations to consequences; do not add prompts to harmless commands.
75	- Add `--dry-run` for consequential mutations using the real validation/plan
76	  path. Do not execute probes with [REDACTED:generic-password] writes or create state during preview.
77	- Provide relevant help examples and shell completion for commands/values.
78	  Keep slow or authenticated discovery out of ordinary help/completion.
79	- A child cannot change its parent shell's cwd. If navigation requires a shell
80	  wrapper, use a narrow structured handoff, not `eval` of general command output.
81	
82	Authentication-required is not a missing wizard field. For SSH, keep background
83	checks noninteractive and let an explicit human action hand the terminal to
84	native SSH; machine output returns a structured requirement. Preserve the draft
85	across cancellation. See [SSH authentication handoffs](async-terminal.md#ssh-authentication-handoffs)
86	for terminal restoration, session lifetime and shared-master ownership.
87	
88	## Wizard experience
89	
90	Use guided choice to remove syntax memorization, not to ask every possible flag.
91	Prefill known values, explain defaults, offer searchable selects for long lists,
92	and reveal advanced choices only when selected or needed. Keep optional fields
93	skippable. Show the current step/task; avoid an inaccurate fixed step count when
94	branches change the flow.
95	
96	Maintain a draft request separate from applied state. Back preserves answers;
97	changing an upstream choice invalidates or revalidates dependent answers.
98	Validate locally on field/step completion, then validate the complete request
99	through the domain service. Errors stay near the field and keep user input.
100
````

22	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, cfg config.Config, request Request, opts Options) (Plan, error) {
23		getenv := opts.Getenv
24		if getenv == nil {
25			getenv = os.Getenv
26		}
27		if request.Endpoint != "" {
28			if request.TargetID != "" {
29				return Plan{}, errors.New("use either --endpoint or --target")
30			}
31			return explicitPlan(request.Endpoint, request.SocksEndpoint, "explicit endpoint")
32		}
33		if request.SocksEndpoint != "" {
34			return Plan{}, errors.New("--socks-endpoint requires --endpoint")
35		}
36		if request.TargetID != "" {
37			for _, target := range cfg.Targets {
38				if target.ID == request.TargetID {
39					return resolveTarget(ctx, target, opts)
40				}
41			}
42			return Plan{}, errors.New("proxy target is not registered; use targets list")
43		}
44		if value := getenv("LOCAL_PROXY_URL"); value != "" {
45			return explicitPlan(value, getenv("LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL"), "LOCAL_PROXY_URL")
46		}
47		var local []config.Target
48		for _, target := range cfg.Targets {
49			if IsLocalTarget(target) {
50				local = append(local, target)
51			}
52		}
53		for _, target := range local {
54			if target.ID == cfg.DefaultTarget {
55				return resolveTarget(ctx, target, opts)
56			}
57		}
58		if len(local) == 0 {
59			discover := opts.Discover
60			if discover == nil {
61				discover = connection.Discover
62			}
63			var err error
64			local, err = discover(ctx, "")
65			if err != nil {
66				return Plan{}, err
67			}
68		}
69		if len(local) == 0 {
70			return Plan{}, ErrNoProxyConfigured
71		}
72		if len(local) > 1 {
73			return Plan{}, &AmbiguousError{Targets: local}
74		}
75		return resolveTarget(ctx, local[0], opts)
76	}
77	
78	func IsLocalTarget(target config.Target) bool {
79		if target.SSHHost != "" {
80			return false
81		}
82		u, err := url.Parse(target.Controller)
83		if err != nil {
84			return false
85		}

88	func loopback(host string) bool {
89		ip := net.ParseIP(host)
90		return strings.EqualFold(host, "localhost") || (ip != nil && ip.IsLoopback())

92	
93	func explicitPlan(endpoint, socks, source string) (Plan, error) {
94		if endpoint == "" {
95			return Plan{}, errors.New("a data proxy endpoint is required")
96		}
97		if err := ValidateEndpoint(endpoint); err != nil {
98			return Plan{}, err
99		}
100		if socks != "" {
101			if err := ValidateEndpoint(socks); err != nil {
102				return Plan{}, err
103			}
104			u, _ := url.Parse(socks)
105			if u.Scheme != "socks5" && u.Scheme != "socks5h" {
106				return Plan{}, errors.New("SOCKS endpoint must use socks5 or socks5h")
107			}
108		} else {
109			socks = endpoint
110		}
111		return Plan{HTTP: endpoint, All: socks, Source: source}, nil
112	}
113	
114	func resolveTarget(ctx context.Context, target config.Target, opts Options) (Plan, error) {
115		var plan Plan
116		var err error
117		if target.ProbeProxy != "" {
118			plan, err = explicitPlan(target.ProbeProxy, "", "registered data proxy")
119		} else {
120			// A remote controller may be behind a reverse proxy. Its hostname is not
121			// evidence that data ports are accessible on that same host.
122			if target.SSHHost == "" && !IsLocalTarget(target) {
123				return plan, errors.New("remote target needs an explicit --probe-proxy endpoint in targets edit")
124			}
125			open := opts.Open
126			if open == nil {
127				open = connection.Open
128			}
129			queryCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 8*time.Second)
130			defer cancel()
131			client, closer, e := open(queryCtx, target, true)
132			if closer != nil {
133				defer closer.Close()
134			}
135			if client != nil {
136				defer client.Close()
137			}
138			if e != nil {
139				return plan, e
140			}
141			if client == nil {
142				return plan, errors.New("controller client unavailable")
143			}
144			runtime, e := client.Config(queryCtx)
145			if e != nil {
146				return plan, e
147			}
148			host := "127.0.0.1"
149			u, _ := url.Parse(target.Controller)
150			if u.Scheme != "unix" && u.Hostname() == "::1" {
151				host = "::1"
152			}
153			port := runtimePort(runtime["mixed-port"])
154			socks := port
155			if port == 0 {
156				port = runtimePort(runtime["port"])
157				socks = runtimePort(runtime["socks-port"])
158			}
159			if port == 0 && socks == 0 {
160				return plan, errors.New("core reports no HTTP/mixed/SOCKS port; configure --probe-proxy explicitly")
161			}
162			endpoint := ""
163			all := ""
164			if port > 0 {
165				endpoint = "http://" + net.JoinHostPort(host, strconv.Itoa(port))
166			}
167			if socks > 0 {
168				all = "socks5h://" + net.JoinHostPort(host, strconv.Itoa(socks))
169			}
170			if endpoint == "" {
171				endpoint = all
172			}
173			plan, err = explicitPlan(endpoint, all, "core runtime ports")
174		}
175		if err != nil {
176			return plan, err
177		}
178		plan.TargetID, plan.SSHHost = target.ID, target.SSHHost
179		plan.Username, plan.PasswordEnv, plan.PasswordFile, plan.CAFile = target.ProbeUsername, target.ProbePasswordEnv, target.ProbePasswordFile, target.ProbeCAFile
180		return plan, nil
181	}
182	func runtimePort(value any) int {
183		var n int
184		switch v := value.(type) {
185		case float64:
186			if v != float64(int(v)) {
187				return 0
188			}
189			n = int(v)
190		case int:
191			n = v
192		case json.Number:
193			n, _ = strconv.Atoi(string(v))
194		case string:
195			n, _ = strconv.Atoi(v)
196		}
197		if n < 1 || n > 65535 {
198			return 0
199		}
200		return n
201	}
202

213			return fmt.Errorf("proxy credentials: %w", err)

216	}

49		defer transport.CloseIdleConnections()

51		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodHead, destination, nil)
52		if err != nil {

54		}
55		started := time.Now()
56		response, err := client.Do(req)
57		public := *u
58		public.RawQuery = ""
59		public.ForceQuery = false

98		result := map[string]string{}

104		} else if runtime.GOOS == "linux" {

118		}
119		allowed := map[string]bool{"HTTPEnable": true, "HTTPProxy": true, "HTTPPort": true, "HTTPSEnable": true, "HTTPSProxy": true, "HTTPSPort": true, "SOCKSEnable": true, "SOCKSProxy": true, "SOCKSPort": true, "ProxyAutoConfigEnable": true}
120		for _, line := range strings.Split(out.String(), "\n") {
121			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, ":")
122			key = strings.TrimSpace(key)

16		result := TestResult{TargetID: target.ID, SampledAt: opts.now()}
17		if err := config.ValidateTarget(target); err != nil {
18			return result, err
19		}
20		result.Route = route(target, target.Controller)
21		open := opts.Open
22		if open == nil {
23			open = connection.Open
24		}
25		started := time.Now()
26		client, closer, err := open(ctx, target, true)
27		if err != nil {
28			result.Milliseconds = float64(time.Since(started)) / float64(time.Millisecond)
29			return result, err
30		}
31		if closer != nil {
32			defer closer.Close()
33		}
34		defer client.Close()
35		version, err := client.Version(ctx)
36		if err == nil {
37			result.Version, _ = version["version"].(string)
38			result.Version = strings.Join(strings.Fields(core.Sanitize(result.Version)), " ")
39			if result.Version == "" {
40				err = &core.Error{Kind: core.KindInvalid, Operation: "identify controller"}
41			}
42		}
43		if err == nil {
44			result.Connected = true
45			_, err = client.Config(ctx)
46			result.ConfigsReadable = err == nil
47		}

15	func (o *options) proxyPlan(cmd *cobra.Command, endpoint, socks, id string) (proxyenv.Plan, error) {

17		if err != nil {

28		}

30			t, _, e := o.choose(cmd, cfg)
31			if e != nil {
32				return proxyenv.Plan{}, e
33			}
34			if t.ID == "" {

36			}

38			id = t.ID
39		}
40		opts := proxyenv.Options{Open: o.deps.Open, Discover: o.deps.Discover}
41		request := proxyenv.Request{TargetID: id, Endpoint: endpoint, SocksEndpoint: socks}
42		p, err := proxyenv.Resolve(cmd.Context(), cfg, request, opts)
43		var authentication *connection.AuthRequiredError
44		foreground := cmd.Name() == "start" || cmd.Name() == "exec" || cmd.Name() == "test"
45		if foreground && errors.As(err, &authentication) && !o.json && o.deps.Terminal(cmd.InOrStdin(), cmd.ErrOrStderr()) {
46			auth, e := o.deps.Authenticate(cmd.Context(), authentication.Host)
47			if e != nil {
48				return p, e
49			}
50			auth.Stdin, auth.Stdout, auth.Stderr = cmd.InOrStdin(), cmd.ErrOrStderr(), cmd.ErrOrStderr()
51			if e = auth.Run(); e != nil {
52				return p, errors.New("SSH authentication failed while resolving data proxy ports")
53			}
54			p, err = proxyenv.Resolve(cmd.Context(), cfg, request, opts)
55		}
56		var ambiguous *proxyenv.AmbiguousError
57		if errors.As(err, &ambiguous) && !o.json && o.deps.Terminal(cmd.InOrStdin(), cmd.ErrOrStderr()) {
58			choices := make([]wizard.Choice, 0, len(ambiguous.Targets))
59			for _, t := range ambiguous.Targets {
60				choices = append(choices, wizard.Choice{Value: t.ID, Label: t.Label() + " · " + t.Controller})
61			}

63			if e != nil {
64				return p, e
65			}
66			cfg.Targets = append(cfg.Targets, ambiguous.Targets...)
67			request.TargetID = selected
68			return proxyenv.Resolve(cmd.Context(), cfg, request, opts)
69		}
70		return p, err
71	}

119	func Analyze(report Report) Report {
120		report.Conflicts = nil
121		report.ExcludedRoutes = nil
122		report.DNSPolicies = map[string][]string{}
123		report.FakeIPFilter = nil
124		add := func(code, level, confidence, message string, evidence ...string) {
125			report.Conflicts = append(report.Conflicts, Finding{code, level, confidence, message, evidence})
126		}
127		excluded := map[string]bool{}
128		addPrefix := func(raw string) {
129			prefix, err := netip.ParsePrefix(raw)
130			if err != nil {
131				if ip, e := netip.ParseAddr(raw); e == nil {
132					prefix = netip.PrefixFrom(ip, ip.BitLen())
133				} else {
134					return
135				}
136			}
137			if prefix.Bits() > 0 {
138				excluded[prefix.Masked().String()] = true
139			}
140		}
141		for _, p := range []string{"127.0.0.0/8", "::1/128"} {
142			addPrefix(p)
143		}
144		if report.ManagementAddress != "" {
145			addPrefix(report.ManagementAddress)
146		}
147		interfaces := map[string]Interface{}
148		for _, iface := range report.Interfaces {
149			interfaces[iface.Name] = iface
150		}
151		if report.Tailscale.Running {
152			addPrefix("100.64.0.0/10")
153			addPrefix("fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48")
154			if suffix := domain(report.Tailscale.Suffix); suffix != "" {
155				report.DNSPolicies["+."+suffix] = []string{"100.100.100.100"}
156				report.FakeIPFilter = append(report.FakeIPFilter, "+."+suffix)
157			}
158			add("tailscale-split", "information", "confirmed", "Review tailnet and accepted subnet exclusions together with MagicDNS settings.")
159		}
160		if report.Tailscale.ExitNode {
161			add("tailscale-exit-node", "conflict", "confirmed", "A Tailscale exit node owns default routing; choose one full-tunnel owner before enabling Mihomo TUN.")
162		}
163		defaultVPN := map[string][]string{}
164		for _, route := range report.Routes {
165			iface := interfaces[route.Interface]
166			vpn := tunnelInterface(route.Interface, iface.Kind)
167			prefix, err := netip.ParsePrefix(route.Destination)
168			full := route.Destination == "default" || (err == nil && prefix.Bits() <= 1)
169			if full && vpn && !route.Scoped {
170				defaultVPN[route.Interface] = append(defaultVPN[route.Interface], route.Destination)
171			}
172			if err != nil || full {
173				continue
174			}
175			// Exclude actual connected private routes and accepted routes through VPNs,
176			// not arbitrary advertised peer prefixes or the whole default route.
177			if (vpn && route.Interface != report.CoreTUNDevice && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(route.Interface), "mihomo")) || (!vpn && prefix.Addr().IsPrivate() && route.Gateway == "") {
178				addPrefix(prefix.String())
179			}
180			if route.Table == "2022" && !report.CoreTUNKnown {
181				add("possible-mihomo-table", "warning", "probable", "Routing table 2022 is present; inspect the existing TUN owner before setup.", route.Interface)
182			}
183		}
184		for iface, routes := range defaultVPN {
185			// One /1 is not evidence for both halves, but is still overlapping global
186			// routing that must be resolved before installing another default route.
187			add("vpn-default-route", "conflict", "confirmed", "An existing tunnel has default or broad /1 routes; choose its routing owner before enabling another TUN.", append([]string{iface}, routes...)...)
188		}
189		for _, resolver := range report.Resolvers {
190			var servers []string
191			for _, server := range resolver.Servers {
192				ip, err := netip.ParseAddr(strings.Split(server, "%")[0])
193				if err != nil {
194					continue
195				}
196				servers = append(servers, server)
197				if ip.IsPrivate() || isTailnetIP(ip) {
198					addPrefix(ip.String())
199				}
200			}
201			for _, suffix := range resolver.Domains {
202				suffix = strings.TrimPrefix(suffix, "~")
203				if suffix == "." {
204					if tunnelInterface(resolver.Interface, interfaces[resolver.Interface].Kind) {
205						add("vpn-default-dns", "warning", "confirmed", "A VPN resolver handles all DNS domains; inspect resolver precedence before enabling DNS interception.", resolver.Interface)
206					}
207					continue
208				}
209				if suffix = domain(suffix); suffix != "" && len(servers) > 0 {
210					key := "+." + suffix
211					report.DNSPolicies[key] = appendUnique(report.DNSPolicies[key], servers...)
212					report.FakeIPFilter = appendUnique(report.FakeIPFilter, key)
213				}
214			}
215		}
216		if report.ExistingTUN {
217			add("existing-core-tun", "conflict", "confirmed", "The observed core already owns TUN; configure that owner instead of starting a second TUN.")
218		}
219		for _, process := range report.Processes {
220			name := strings.ToLower(process)
221			if strings.Contains(name, "safeconnect") || strings.Contains(name, "openvpn") || strings.Contains(name, "openconnect") || strings.Contains(name, "vpnagent") || strings.Contains(name, "forti") || strings.Contains(name, "globalprotect") || strings.Contains(name, "charon") {
222				add("vpn-client-present", "warning", "probable", "A VPN client is running; process presence alone does not prove interception or compatibility.", process)
223			}
224		}
225		for _, capability := range report.Capabilities {
226			if !capability.Available {
227				add("inventory-unavailable", "warning", "unknown", "Some network evidence is unavailable; an empty result is not proof of no conflict.", capability.Name, capability.Detail)
228			}
229		}
230		for p := range excluded {
231			prefix, _ := netip.ParsePrefix(p)
232			covered := false
233			for other := range excluded {
234				parent, _ := netip.ParsePrefix(other)
235				if parent.Bits() < prefix.Bits() && parent.Contains(prefix.Addr()) {
236					covered = true
237					break
238				}
239			}
240			if !covered {
241				report.ExcludedRoutes = append(report.ExcludedRoutes, p)
242			}
243		}
244		sort.Strings(report.ExcludedRoutes)
245		sort.Strings(report.FakeIPFilter)
246		sort.SliceStable(report.Conflicts, func(i, j int) bool {
247			a, b := report.Conflicts[i], report.Conflicts[j]
248			return a.Code+strings.Join(a.Evidence, ",") < b.Code+strings.Join(b.Evidence, ",")
249		})
250		return report
251	}

1	// Package connection resolves target credentials and owns the transports it opens.
2	package connection
3	
4	import (
5		"context"
6		"errors"
7		"fmt"
8		"io"
9		"net"
10		"net/url"
11		"os"
12		"strings"
13		"time"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/lazyclash/internal/config"
16		"github.com/daviddwlee84/lazyclash/internal/core"
17	)
18	
19	type closerFunc func() error
20	
21	func (f closerFunc) Close() error { return f() }
22	
23	// Open never falls back to a different target. Secrets are resolved only from
24	// references on this target, and are never passed to SSH or another process.
25	func Open(ctx context.Context, target config.Target, readOnly bool) (*core.Client, io.Closer, error) {
26		if err := config.ValidateTarget(target); err != nil {
27			return nil, nil, err
28		}
29		[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], err := resolveSecret(ctx, target)
30		if err != nil {
31			return nil, nil, err
32		}
33		opts := core.Options{Endpoint: target.Controller, Secret: [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], CAFile: target.CAFile, ReadOnly: readOnly}
34		var closer io.Closer = closerFunc(func() error { return nil })
35		if target.SSHHost != "" {
36			u, _ := url.Parse(target.Controller)
37			if u.Scheme == "unix" {
38				return nil, nil, errors.New("remote Unix controller sockets are not supported; expose a loopback HTTP(S) controller on the SSH host")
39			}
40			tunnel, err := openTunnel(ctx, target.SSHHost, u)
41			if err != nil {
42				return nil, nil, err
43			}
44			closer = tunnel
45			opts.DialContext = func(ctx context.Context, network, address string) (net.Conn, error) {
46				return (&net.Dialer{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}).DialContext(ctx, "tcp", tunnel.address)
47			}
48		}
49		client, err := core.New(opts)
50		if err != nil {
51			_ = closer.Close()
52			return nil, nil, err
53		}
54		version, err := client.Version(ctx)
55		if err == nil {
56			if v, ok := version["version"].(string); !ok || v == "" {
57				err = &core.Error{Kind: core.KindInvalid, Operation: "identify controller"}
58			}
59		}
60		if err != nil {
61			_ = client.Close()
62			_ = closer.Close()
63			return nil, nil, err
64		}
65		transportCloser := closer
66		return client, closerFunc(func() error { _ = client.Close(); return transportCloser.Close() }), nil
67	}
68	
69	func resolveSecret(ctx context.Context, t config.Target) (string, error) {
70		if t.SecretEnv != "" {
71			[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], ok := os.LookupEnv(t.SecretEnv)
72			if !ok {
73				return "", fmt.Errorf("[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] environment variable %s is not set", t.SecretEnv)
74			}
75			return cleanSecret([REDACTED:generic-credential-uri])
76		}
77		if t.SecretFile != "" {
78			data, err := readLimitedFile(t.SecretFile, 64*1024)
79			if err != nil {
80				return "", errors.New("cannot read configured local [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] file")
81			}
82			return cleanSecret(strings.TrimRight(string(data), "\r\n"))
83		}
84		if t.SourceConfig != "" {
85			var data []byte
86			var err error
87			if t.SSHHost != "" {
88				data, err = remoteRead(ctx, t.SSHHost, t.SourceConfig)
89			} else {
90				data, err = readLimitedFile(t.SourceConfig, maxConfigBytes)
91			}
92			if err != nil {
93				if IsAuthRequired(err) {
94					return "", err
95				}
96				return "", errors.New("cannot read this target's source_config; fix its path or configure [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]_env/[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]_file")
97			}
98			runtime, err := parseRuntime(data)
99			if err != nil {
100				return "", errors.New("invalid YAML in this target's source_config")
101			}
102			if !runtime.matches(t.Controller) {
103				return "", errors.New("source_config controller no longer matches this target; rediscover or configure an explicit [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] reference")
104			}
105			return cleanSecret(runtime.Secret)
106		}
107		return cleanSecret(t.Secret)
108	}
109	
110	func cleanSecret(s string) (string, error) {
111		if strings.ContainsAny(s, "\r\n\x00") {
112			return "", errors.New("controller [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] contains invalid control characters")
113		}
114		return s, nil
115	}
116	
117	func readLimitedFile(path string, limit int64) ([]byte, error) {
118		f, err := os.Open(path)
119		if err != nil {
120			return nil, err
121		}
122		defer f.Close()
123		info, err := f.Stat()
124		if err != nil {
125			return nil, err
126		}
127		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
128			return nil, errors.New("expected a regular file")
129		}
130		data, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(f, limit+1))
131		if err != nil {
132			return nil, err
133		}
134		if int64(len(data)) > limit {
135			return nil, errors.New("file exceeds size limit")
136		}
137		return data, nil
138	}
139

17	// SystemProxyScript is fixed, caller-owned host code. A privileged executor may
18	// exec it with __name__='lazyclash_system_proxy' and call apply_plan(plan,restore).
19	// The plan contains typed states, never arbitrary commands.
20	//
21	//go:embed system_proxy.py
22	var SystemProxyScript string
23	
24	type ProxyListener struct {
25		Enabled       bool   `json:"enabled"`
26		Host          string `json:"host"`
27		Port          int    `json:"port"`
28		Authenticated bool   `json:"authenticated"`
29	}
30	type SystemProxyState struct {
31		Service    string        `json:"service"`
32		HTTP       ProxyListener `json:"http"`
33		HTTPS      ProxyListener `json:"https"`
34		SOCKS      ProxyListener `json:"socks"`
35		PACEnabled bool          `json:"pac_enabled"`
36		PACURL     string        `json:"pac_url"`
37		Discovery  bool          `json:"discovery"`
38		Exceptions []string      `json:"exceptions"`
39		Mode       string        `json:"mode,omitempty"`
40	}
41	type SystemProxySnapshot struct {
42		Protocol          int                `json:"protocol"`
43		OS                string             `json:"os"`
44		Backend           string             `json:"backend"`
45		SelectionExplicit bool               `json:"selection_explicit"`
46		Services          []SystemProxyState `json:"services"`
47		Unavailable       string             `json:"unavailable,omitempty"`
48	}
49	type SystemProxyChange struct {
50		Service string           `json:"service"`
51		Before  SystemProxyState `json:"before"`
52		After   SystemProxyState `json:"after"`
53	}
54	type SystemProxyPlan struct {
55		OS      string              `json:"os"`
56		Backend string              `json:"backend"`
57		Changes []SystemProxyChange `json:"changes"`
58	}
59	
60	func ReadSystemProxy(ctx context.Context, sshHost string, services []string) (SystemProxySnapshot, error) {
61		for _, service := range services {
62			if !safeService(service) {
63				return SystemProxySnapshot{}, errors.New("invalid system proxy network service")
64			}
65		}
66		request, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"op": "read", "services": services})
67		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 40*time.Second)
68		defer cancel()
69		data, err := connection.ExecutePython(ctx, sshHost, SystemProxyScript, request, 256<<10)
70		if err != nil {
71			return SystemProxySnapshot{}, err
72		}
73		var snapshot SystemProxySnapshot
74		if json.Unmarshal(data, &snapshot) != nil || snapshot.Protocol != 1 {
75			return snapshot, errors.New("system proxy reader returned an unsupported response")
76		}
77		return snapshot, nil
78	}
79	func PlanSystemProxy(snapshot SystemProxySnapshot, endpoint string, exceptions []string) (SystemProxyPlan, error) {
80		return PlanSystemProxyWithSOCKS(snapshot, endpoint, "", exceptions)
81	}
82	func PlanSystemProxyWithSOCKS(snapshot SystemProxySnapshot, endpoint, socks string, exceptions []string) (SystemProxyPlan, error) {
83		plan := SystemProxyPlan{OS: snapshot.OS, Backend: snapshot.Backend}
84		if snapshot.Unavailable != "" || len(snapshot.Services) == 0 {
85			return plan, errors.New("system proxy settings are unavailable in this host/session")
86		}
87		if snapshot.Backend != "macos-networksetup" && snapshot.Backend != "gnome-gsettings" {
88			return plan, errors.New("unsupported system proxy backend")
89		}
90		if snapshot.Backend == "macos-networksetup" && !snapshot.SelectionExplicit {
91			return plan, errors.New("select explicit macOS Network services before changing system proxy")
92		}
93		listener := func(value string, schemes ...string) (ProxyListener, error) {
94			u, err := url.Parse(value)
95			if err != nil || u.Hostname() == "" || u.User != nil || u.Path != "" || u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "" {
96				return ProxyListener{}, errors.New("system proxy requires a credential-free host URL with an explicit port")
97			}
98			found := false
99			for _, scheme := range schemes {
100				found = found || u.Scheme == scheme
101			}
102			port, err := strconv.Atoi(u.Port())
103			if !found || err != nil || port < 1 || port > 65535 {
104				return ProxyListener{}, errors.New("system proxy listener scheme or port is unsupported")
105			}
106			return ProxyListener{Enabled: true, Host: u.Hostname(), Port: port}, nil
107		}
108		http, err := listener(endpoint, "http")
109		if err != nil {
110			return plan, err
111		}
112		var socksListener ProxyListener
113		if socks != "" {
114			socksListener, err = listener(socks, "socks5", "socks5h")
115			if err != nil {
116				return plan, err
117			}
118		}
119		for _, exception := range exceptions {
120			if exception == "" || len(exception) > 253 || strings.IndexFunc(exception, unicode.IsControl) >= 0 {
121				return plan, errors.New("invalid system proxy bypass entry")
122			}
123		}
124		for _, before := range snapshot.Services {
125			if before.Exceptions == nil {
126				before.Exceptions = []string{}
127			}
128			if !safeService(before.Service) {
129				return plan, errors.New("invalid system proxy network service")
130			}
131			if before.HTTP.Authenticated || before.HTTPS.Authenticated || before.SOCKS.Authenticated {
132				return plan, errors.New("an existing authenticated system proxy cannot be safely snapshotted; manage it through its native owner")
133			}
134			after := before
135			after.HTTP, after.HTTPS, after.SOCKS = http, http, socksListener
136			after.PACEnabled, after.Discovery = false, false
137			after.Mode = "manual"
138			after.Exceptions = appendUnique(append([]string{}, before.Exceptions...), exceptions...)
139			plan.Changes = append(plan.Changes, SystemProxyChange{before.Service, before, after})
140		}

20	func TestConnectivityAlwaysReadOnlyAndChecksConfigAccess(t *testing.T) {

23				var configReads, closed atomic.Int32
24				server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
25					if r.Method != "GET" {
26						t.Errorf("diagnostic write: %s", r.Method)
27						w.WriteHeader(500)
28						return
29					}
30					switch r.URL.Path {
31					case "/version":
32						fmt.Fprint(w, `{"version":"v1.19.29"}`)
33					case "/configs":
34						configReads.Add(1)
35						if denied {
36							w.WriteHeader(403)
37						} else {
38							fmt.Fprint(w, `{"mode":"rule","[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]":"never-return-config-body"}`)
39						}
40					default:
41						t.Errorf("unexpected resource %s", r.URL.Path)
42						w.WriteHeader(404)
43					}
44				}))
45				defer server.Close()
46				opts := Options{Open: func(ctx context.Context, target config.Target, readOnly bool) (*core.Client, io.Closer, error) {
47					if !readOnly {
48						t.Error("connectivity opened a writable core client")
49					}
50					client, closer, err := connection.Open(ctx, target, readOnly)
51					if err != nil {
52						return nil, nil, err
53					}
54					return client, closeFunc(func() error { closed.Add(1); return closer.Close() }), nil
55				}}
56				result, err := Test(context.Background(), config.Target{ID: "test", Controller: server.URL}, opts)
57				if (err != nil) != denied || !result.Connected || result.ConfigsReadable == denied || result.Version != "v1.19.29" {
58					t.Fatalf("result=%+v err=%v", result, err)
59				}
60				if configReads.Load() != 1 || closed.Load() != 1 {
61					t.Fatalf("reads=%d closes=%d", configReads.Load(), closed.Load())
62				}
63			})
