60			result.Capabilities = append(result.Capabilities, networkcheck.Capability{Name: safeText(capability.Name), Available: capability.Available})
61			available = available || capability.Available
62			missing = missing || !capability.Available
63		}
64		for _, iface := range snapshot.Interfaces {
65			result.Interfaces = append(result.Interfaces, safeText(iface.Name))
66		}
67		for _, route := range snapshot.Routes {
68			if route.Destination != "default" && route.Destination != "0.0.0.0/0" && route.Destination != "::/0" {
69				continue
70			}
71			result.DefaultRoutes = append(result.DefaultRoutes, networkcheck.Route{Destination: route.Destination, Gateway: safeText(route.Gateway), Interface: safeText(route.Interface), Scoped: route.Scoped})
72		}
73		seen := map[string]bool{}
74		for _, resolver := range snapshot.Resolvers {
75			for _, server := range resolver.Servers {
76				// Retain numeric DNS evidence, not search domains, URLs or tokens.
77				ip, _, _ := strings.Cut(server, "%")
78				if net.ParseIP(ip) != nil && !seen[server] {
79					result.DNSServers = append(result.DNSServers, safeText(server))
80					seen[server] = true
81				}
82			}
83		}
84		check := Check{ID: "network", Status: Pass, Message: "Collected passive interface, default-route and DNS evidence; no DNS query or outbound probe was sent."}
85		if !available {
86			check.Status = Unknown
87			check.Message = "Host inventory has no available capabilities; unsupported is not disabled."
88		} else if missing {
89			check.Status = Warn
90			check.Message = "Collected partial host evidence; some optional host tools are unavailable."
91		}
92		updates <- func(r *Report) { r.Network = &result; r.set(check) }
93	}
94	
95	func compare(r *Report) {
96		check := Check{ID: "consistency", Status: Unknown, Message: "Runtime listener evidence is unavailable; endpoint consistency could not be compared."}
97		if !r.Selection.Local || r.Runtime == nil || !r.Runtime.IdentityVerified {
98			r.set(check)
99			return
100		}
101		for _, current := range r.Checks {
102			if current.ID == "runtime" && current.Status != Pass {
103				r.set(check)
104				return
105			}
106		}
107		if r.Runtime.MixedPort == 0 && r.Runtime.HTTPPort == 0 && r.Runtime.SOCKSPort == 0 {
108			check.Status, check.Message = Skip, "No runtime HTTP/SOCKS listeners to compare. TUN-only operation is valid; egress remains untested."
109			r.set(check)
110			return
111		}
112		want := runtimeEndpoint(config.Target{Controller: r.Selection.Controller}, *r.Runtime)
113		mismatch := false
114		compared := 0
115		consider := func(value, expected string) {
116			if value == "" {
117				return
118			}
119			u, err := url.Parse(value)
120			if err != nil || !proxyenv.IsLocalTarget(config.Target{Controller: value}) {
121				return
122			}
123			if u.Scheme != "http" && u.Scheme != "https" && u.Scheme != "socks5" && u.Scheme != "socks5h" {
124				return
125			}
126			compared++
127			if !sameListener(value, expected) {
128				mismatch = true
129			}
130		}
131		for key, value := range r.Environment.Variables {
132			expected := want.HTTP
133			if strings.HasPrefix(value, "socks") {
134				expected = want.SOCKS
135			}
136			if strings.EqualFold(key, "all_proxy") && expected == "" {
137				expected = want.SOCKS
138			}
139			consider(value, expected)
140		}
141		if r.SystemProxy != nil {
142			for _, service := range r.SystemProxy.Services {
143				consider(service.HTTP, want.HTTP)
144				consider(service.HTTPS, want.HTTP)
145				consider(service.SOCKS, want.SOCKS)
146			}
147		}
148		if r.DataEndpoint.Source != "core runtime ports" {
149			expected := want.HTTP
150			if strings.HasPrefix(r.DataEndpoint.HTTP, "socks") {
151				expected = want.SOCKS
152			}
153			consider(r.DataEndpoint.HTTP, expected)
154			consider(r.DataEndpoint.SOCKS, want.SOCKS)
155		}
156		check.Status = Pass
157		check.Message = "Same-host proxy endpoints match the runtime listener ports; ownership and egress are not established."
158		if compared == 0 {
159			check.Status = Skip
160			check.Message = "No comparable local proxy endpoints were observed; missing environment/system proxy settings alone are not a failure."
161		}
162		if mismatch {
163			check.Status = Warn
164			check.Message = "Some local proxy endpoints differ from this controller's runtime listeners; another proxy or inactive service may explain the difference."
165			check.Suggestion = "Review process proxy variables and active OS network service settings before changing anything; doctor does not establish ownership."
166		}
167		r.set(check)
168	}
169	
170	func sameListener(a, b string) bool {
171		x, errX := url.Parse(a)
172		y, errY := url.Parse(b)
173		if errX != nil || errY != nil || x.Hostname() == "" || y.Hostname() == "" {
174			return false
175		}
176		// localhost is intentionally family-neutral; do not resolve DNS to compare.
177		xHost, yHost := strings.ToLower(x.Hostname()), strings.ToLower(y.Hostname())
178		hostMatches := xHost == yHost || xHost == "localhost" || yHost == "localhost"
179		port := func(u *url.URL) string {
180			if u.Port() != "" {
181				return u.Port()
182			}
183			if u.Scheme == "http" {
184				return "80"
185			}
186			if u.Scheme == "https" {
187				return "443"
188			}
189			return "1080"
190		}
191		return hostMatches && port(x) == port(y)
192	}
193	
194	// Format is a plain-text rendering of the same safe report used for JSON.
195	func Format(r Report) string {
196		var b strings.Builder
197		b.WriteString("Doctor — local, passive (no state changes)\n")
198		if r.Selection.Controller != "" {
199			b.WriteString("Controller: " + r.Selection.Controller + " (" + r.Selection.Source + ")\n")
200		}
201		if r.DataEndpoint.Source != "" {
202			b.WriteString("Data endpoint: " + r.DataEndpoint.HTTP + " " + r.DataEndpoint.SOCKS + " (" + r.DataEndpoint.Source + "; untested)\n")
203		}
204		if r.Runtime != nil {
205			tun := "unknown"
206			if r.Runtime.TUNKnown {
207				tun = strconv.FormatBool(r.Runtime.TUNEnabled)
208			}
209			b.WriteString("Runtime: mode=" + r.Runtime.Mode + " mixed=" + strconv.Itoa(r.Runtime.MixedPort) + " http=" + strconv.Itoa(r.Runtime.HTTPPort) + " socks=" + strconv.Itoa(r.Runtime.SOCKSPort) + " TUN=" + tun + " " + r.Runtime.TUNDevice + "\n")
210		}
211		keys := make([]string, 0, len(r.Environment.Variables))
212		for key := range r.Environment.Variables {
213			keys = append(keys, key)
214		}
215		sort.Strings(keys)
216		for _, key := range keys {
217			b.WriteString("Environment: " + key + "=" + r.Environment.Variables[key] + "\n")
218		}
219		if r.SystemProxy != nil {
220			for _, service := range r.SystemProxy.Services {
221				b.WriteString("System proxy: " + service.Name + " http=" + service.HTTP + " https=" + service.HTTPS + " socks=" + service.SOCKS + " PAC=" + strconv.FormatBool(service.PACEnabled) + "\n")
222			}
223		}
224		for _, check := range r.Checks {
225			b.WriteString("[" + string(check.Status) + "] " + check.ID + ": " + check.Message + "\n")
226		}
227		if r.Summary.Canceled {
228			b.WriteString("Canceled; partial results above.\n")
229		} else if r.Summary.TimedOut {
230			b.WriteString("Overall timeout reached; partial results above.\n")
231		}
232		for _, suggestion := range r.Suggestions {
233			b.WriteString("Next: " + suggestion + "\n")
234		}
235		b.WriteString("Exit status: " + strconv.Itoa(r.Summary.ExitCode) + "\n")
236		return b.String()
237	}

not the test suite, not an `import` of an internal function and a

window.

## First: does a project skill already cover this?

A project skill that launches this app is the repo's verified path -
its author already cold-started from a Linux container and committed
what worked: the exact `apt-get` line, the env vars, the patches, the
driver. Use it instead of rediscovering.

```bash
d=$PWD; while :; do

  [ -e "$d/.git" ] || [ "$d" = / ] && break

done

- **One describes launching/driving this app** -> read that SKILL.md

## Otherwise: match the shape, use the pattern

Pick the row closest to your project. Each example walks through
launch + first interaction; ignore any trailing "write the skill"
section - you're using the recipe, not authoring one.

| Project type | Handle | Example |
|---|---|---|
| CLI tool | direct invocation, exit code, stdin/stdout | [examples/cli.md](examples/cli.md) |
| Web server / API | background launch + `curl` smoke | [examples/server.md](examples/server.md) |
| TUI / interactive terminal | tmux `send-keys` / `capture-pane` | [examples/tui.md](examples/tui.md) |
| Electron / desktop GUI | Playwright `_electron` REPL under xvfb | [examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) |
| Browser-driven | dev server + `chromium-cli` script | [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) |
| Library / SDK | import-and-call smoke script at the package boundary | [examples/library.md](examples/library.md) |

If nothing fits, start from the closest match and adapt. For a web
app, [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) - drive it with
`chromium-cli`, no custom driver needed. For a desktop app,
[examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) - it has the `_electron`
REPL driver skeleton and the tmux wrapping.

## Drive it, don't just launch it

Launching with no interaction proves the entrypoint resolves. That's
not running the app - it's typechecking with extra steps. Drive it to
a point where a user would see something:

- CLI -> type a representative command, check the exit code and output.
- Server -> hit the route the diff touches with `curl`, read the body.
- TUI -> `send-keys` a navigation, `capture-pane` the result.
- GUI -> click the button, screenshot the window. **Look at the
  screenshot.** A blank frame is a failure to launch.

If the fallback pattern didn't work out of the box - you had to
install packages, set env vars, patch config, or write a driver -
recommend `/run-skill-generator` in your report so that work gets
captured as a project skill. If it just worked, don't.

```go
//go:build unix

package vps

import (
	"errors"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"syscall"
	"time"
)

// Cloud CLIs may be shell wrappers (Homebrew az starts a Python child).
// Cancel the invocation's own process group, not just the wrapper: descendants
// otherwise retain stdout and make exec.Wait outlive the operation deadline.
// This follows the process-group pattern used by brewupgrade/selfupdate.
func configureCLICommand(cmd *exec.Cmd) {
	cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}
	cmd.Cancel = func() error {
		err := syscall.Kill(-cmd.Process.Pid, syscall.SIGKILL)
		if errors.Is(err, syscall.ESRCH) {
			return os.ErrProcessDone
		}
		return err
	}
	cmd.WaitDelay = 2 * time.Second
}

```

//go:build unix

package vps

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

func TestRunCLICancelsWrapperAndInheritedOutput(t *testing.T) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 150*time.Millisecond)
	defer cancel()
	started := time.Now()
	// The shell waits for a child which also holds stdout. Killing just the
	// shell reproduces the real Homebrew az timeout that stranded its Python.
	_, err := runCLI(ctx, "sh", []string{"-c", "sleep 4 & wait"})
	if !errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
		t.Fatalf("expected deadline, got %v", err)
	}
	if elapsed := time.Since(started); elapsed > 2*time.Second {
		t.Fatalf("child retained command output after cancellation: %s", elapsed)
	}
}

func TestRunCLIRetainsSuccessfulOutput(t *testing.T) {
	data, err := runCLI(context.Background(), "sh", []string{"-c", "printf '{\"ok\":true}'"})
	if err != nil || string(data) != `{"ok":true}` {
		t.Fatalf("output=%q error=%v", data, err)
	}
}

415:Adding component object model (COM) ports require that you disable Secure Boot. COM ports are disabled by default in Trusted Launch VMs.

434-### I'm currently using Gen2 VM or scale set without Trusted Launch and would like to continue using Non-Trusted Launch configuration after the TLaD general availability
435-
436:Trusted Launch VMs provide you with foundational compute security at no extra cost. We strongly recommend that you don't disable them for new VM or scale set deployments. Reach out to us at [Trusted launch default feedback](https://aka.ms/TrustedLaunchDefault/Feedback).
437-
438:See [Can I disable Trusted launch for new deployment](trusted-launch-faq#can-i-disable-trusted-launch-for-a-new-vm-deployment) if you explicitly need to disable Trusted launch.

450-For managed images, use [Azure Compute Gallery](azure-compute-gallery) for the latest capabilities. All new features, like ARM64, Trusted Launch, and Confidential VM are only supported through Azure Compute Gallery.
451-
452:### Can I disable Trusted Launch for a new VM deployment?
453-
454:Trusted Launch VMs provide you with foundational compute security. We **strongly** recommend that you don't disable them for new VM or scale set deployments except if your deployments have dependency on:
455-
456-- [A VM size currently not supported](trusted-launch#virtual-machines-sizes)
457-- [Unsupported features with Trusted Launch](trusted-launch#unsupported-features)
458-- [An OS that doesn't support Trusted Launch](trusted-launch#operating-systems-supported)
459-- [VM used to generate TrustedLaunchSupported Azure compute gallery image](trusted-launch-portal#trusted-launch-vm-supported-images)
460-
461:To disable Trusted Launch in new VM or scale set deployments, use the `securityType` parameter with the `Standard` value by using Microsoft.Compute API version 2025-11-01+, Azure PowerShell (v15.6.1+), and the Azure CLI (v2.86.0+).
462-
463-Note

466-
467:If you need to disable Secure Boot, under the VM's configuration, clear the **Enable Secure Boot** option.

# Trusted Launch for Azure VMs - Azure Virtual Machines | Microsoft Learn

**Applies to:** ✔️ Linux VMs ✔️ Windows VMs ✔️ Flexible scale sets ✔️ Uniform scale sets

Azure Trusted Launch provides an easy way to improve the security of [Generation 2](generation-2) virtual machines (VMs). Trusted Launch protects against advanced and persistent attack techniques by providing enhanced protection against bootkits, rootkits, and low-level malware attacks. It uses several coordinated infrastructure technologies that you can enable independently. Each technology adds another layer of defense against sophisticated threats.

Trusted Launch is supported for both x64 and Arm64 architectures.

Important

- Trusted Launch is the default state for newly created Azure Gen2 VM and scale sets. See the [Trusted Launch FAQs](trusted-launch-faq) if your new VM requires features that [aren't supported with Trusted launch](trusted-launch#unsupported-features).
- You can upgrade existing Azure Gen1 VMs to Gen2-Trusted launch to enable Secure Boot and vTPM. See [Upgrade existing Gen1 VMs to Gen2-Trusted launch](trusted-launch-existing-vm-gen-1).
- [Existing VMs](overview) can have Trusted Launch enabled after being created. For more information, see [Enable Trusted Launch on existing Gen2 VMs](trusted-launch-existing-vm).
- Existing [virtual machine scale sets](../virtual-machine-scale-sets/overview) can have Trusted Launch enabled after being created. For more information, see [Enable Trusted Launch on existing scale set](trusted-launch-existing-vmss).

## Benefits

- Securely deploy VMs with verified boot loaders, operating system (OS) kernels, and drivers.
- Securely protect keys, certificates, and [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]s in the VMs.
- Gain insights and confidence of the entire boot chain's integrity.
- Ensure that workloads are trusted and verifiable.

Plan to transition off HC-series well before the retirement date to avoid disruption.

Note

- Installation of the *CUDA & GRID drivers on Secure Boot-enabled Windows VMs* doesn't require any extra steps.
- Installation of the *CUDA driver on Secure Boot-enabled Ubuntu VMs* requires extra steps. For more information, see [Install NVIDIA GPU drivers on N-series VMs running Linux](linux/n-series-driver-setup#cuda-drivers). Secure Boot should be disabled for installing CUDA drivers on other Linux VMs.
- Installation of the *GRID driver* requires Secure Boot to be disabled for Linux VMs.
- *Not supported* size families don't support [Generation 2](generation-2) VMs. Change the VM size to equivalent *supported size families* for enabling Trusted Launch.

## More information

**Regions**:

- All public regions
- All Azure Government regions
- All Azure China regions

**Pricing**: Trusted Launch doesn't increase existing VM pricing costs.

## Unsupported features

Currently, the following VM features aren't supported with Trusted Launch:

- [Managed Image](capture-image-resource) (customers are encouraged to use [Azure Compute Gallery](trusted-launch-portal#trusted-launch-vm-supported-images)).
- [Linux VM Hibernation](linux/hibernate-resume-linux)

## Secure Boot

At the root of Trusted Launch is Secure Boot for your VM. Secure Boot, which is implemented in platform firmware, protects against the execution of malware-based rootkits and boot kits. Secure Boot works to ensure that only signed operating systems and drivers can boot. It establishes a "root of trust" for the software stack on your VM.

With Secure Boot enabled, all OS boot components (boot loader, kernel, kernel drivers) require trusted publishers signing. Both Windows and major Linux distributions support Secure Boot. If Secure Boot fails to authenticate that the image is signed by a trusted publisher, the VM fails to boot. For more information, see [Secure Boot](/en-us/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/oem-secure-boot).

## vTPM

Trusted Launch also introduces virtual Trusted Platform Module (vTPM) for Azure VMs. This virtualized version of a hardware [Trusted Platform Module](/en-us/windows/security/information-protection/tpm/trusted-platform-module-overview) is compliant with the TPM2.0 spec. It serves as a dedicated secure vault for keys and measurements.

Trusted Launch provides your VM with its own dedicated TPM instance that runs in a secure environment outside the reach of any VM. The vTPM enables [attestation](/en-us/windows/security/information-protection/tpm/tpm-fundamentals#measured-boot-with-support-for-attestation) by measuring the entire boot chain of your VM (UEFI, OS, system, and drivers).

Trusted Launch uses the vTPM to perform remote attestation through the cloud. Attestations enable platform health checks and are used for making trust-based decisions. As a health check, Trusted Launch can cryptographically certify that your VM booted correctly.

If the process fails, possibly because your VM is running an unauthorized component, Microsoft Defender for Cloud issues integrity alerts. The alerts include details on which components failed to pass integrity checks.

## Virtualization-based security

[Virtualization-based security](/en-us/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/oem-vbs) (VBS) uses the hypervisor to create a secure and isolated region of memory. Windows uses these regions to run various security solutions with increased protection against vulnerabilities and malicious exploits. Trusted Launch lets you enable hypervisor code integrity (HVCI) and Windows Defender Credential Guard.

HVCI is a powerful system mitigation that protects Windows kernel-mode processes against injection and execution of malicious or unverified code. It checks kernel mode drivers and binaries before they run, preventing unsigned files from loading into memory. Checks ensure that executable code can't be modified after it's allowed by HVCI to load. For more information about VBS and HVCI, see [Virtualization-based security and hypervisor-enforced code integrity](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/windows-insider-program/virtualization-based-security-vbs-and-hypervisor-enforced-code/m-p/240571).

With Trusted Launch and VBS, you can enable Windows Defender Credential Guard. Credential Guard isolates and protects [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]s so that only privileged system software can access them. It helps prevent unauthorized access to [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]s and credential theft attacks, like Pass-the-Hash attacks. For more information, see [Credential Guard](/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/credential-guard/credential-guard).

## Microsoft Defender for Cloud integration

Trusted Launch is integrated with Defender for Cloud to ensure that your VMs are properly configured. Defender for Cloud continually assesses compatible VMs and issues relevant recommendations:

- **Recommendation to enable Secure Boot**: The Secure Boot recommendation only applies for VMs that support Trusted Launch. Defender for Cloud identifies VMs that have Secure boot disabled. It issues a low-severity recommendation to enable it.
- **Recommendation to enable vTPM**: If vTPM is enabled for VM, Defender for Cloud can use it to perform guest attestation and identify advanced threat patterns. If Defender for Cloud identifies VMs that support Trusted Launch with vTPM disabled, it issues a low-severity recommendation to enable it.
- **Recommendation to install guest attestation extension**: If your VM has Secure Boot and vTPM enabled but it doesn't have the Guest Attestation extension installed, Defender for Cloud issues low-severity recommendations to install the Guest Attestation extension on it. This extension allows Defender for Cloud to proactively attest and monitor the boot integrity of your VMs. Boot integrity is attested via remote attestation.
- **Attestation health assessment or boot integrity monitoring**: If your VM has Secure Boot and vTPM enabled and the Attestation extension installed, Defender for Cloud can remotely validate that your VM booted in a healthy way. This practice is known as boot integrity monitoring. Defender for Cloud issues an assessment that indicates the status of remote attestation.

    If your VMs are properly set up with Trusted Launch, Defender for Cloud can detect and alert you of VM health problems.
- **Alert for VM attestation failure**: Defender for Cloud periodically performs attestation on your VMs. The attestation also happens after your VM boots. If the attestation fails, it triggers a medium-severity alert.

    Note

    VM client boot attestation alerts surfaced in Microsoft Defender for Cloud are informational and are not currently presented in the Defender portal.

    VM attestation can fail for the following reasons:

    - The attested information, which includes a boot log, deviates from a trusted baseline. Any deviation can indicate that untrusted modules are loaded, and the OS could be compromised.
    - The attestation quote couldn't be verified to originate from the vTPM of the attested VM. An unverified origin can indicate that malware is present and could be intercepting traffic to the vTPM.

        Note

        Alerts are available for VMs with vTPM enabled and the Attestation extension installed. Secure Boot must be enabled for attestation to pass. Attestation fails if Secure Boot is disabled. If you must disable Secure Boot, you can suppress this alert to avoid false positives.
- **Alert for untrusted Linux kernel module**: For Trusted Launch with Secure Boot enabled, it's possible for a VM to boot even if a kernel driver fails validation and is prohibited from loading. If kernel driver validation failure happens, Defender for Cloud issues low-severity alerts. While there's no immediate threat, because the untrusted driver didn't load, these events should be investigated. Ask yourself:

    - Which kernel driver failed? Am I familiar with the failed kernel driver and do I expect it to load?
    - Is the exact version of the driver same as expected? Are the driver binaries intact? If failed driver is a partner driver, did the partner pass the OS compliance tests to get it signed?

## (General Availability) Trusted Launch as default

Important

Trusted Launch as Default is generally available for new Gen2 virtual machines (VMs) and virtual machine scale sets (scale sets). TLaD is a fast and zero-touch means of improving the security posture of new Gen2 based Azure VM and virtual machine scale sets deployments. When you register the subscription for this feature, Trusted Launch as Default sets any new Gen2 VMs or scale sets that you create through any client tools (like ARM template, Bicep, Terraform) to Trusted Launch VMs with secure boot and vTPM enabled by default. This change doesn't override inputs provided as part of the deployment code.

Azure portal, PowerShell, and CLI customers get Trusted Launch enabled by default.

### Enable TLaD (Trusted Launch as default)

To make this feature available for all VMs you create for your workloads by default, first register the feature `TrustedLaunchByDefaultPreview` under the `Microsoft.Compute` namespace on your virtual machine subscription. For more information, see [Set up preview features in Azure subscription](/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/preview-features).

To create a new Gen2 VM or scale set with Trusted Launch default, run your existing deployment script through Azure SDK, Terraform, or another method.

Note

Creating VMs defaults to Trusted Launch for Azure portal, CLI, or PowerShell regardless of registering the feature.

### VM and scale set deployments with TLaD

#### Existing behavior

To create Trusted launch VM & scale set, you need to add following securityProfile element in deployment:

```json
"securityProfile": {
    "securityType": "TrustedLaunch",
    "uefiSettings": {
        "secureBootEnabled": true,
        "vTpmEnabled": true,
    }
}
```

Absence of securityProfile element in deployment code deploys VM & scale set without enabling Trusted launch.

**Examples**

- [vm-windows-admincenter](https://github.com/Azure/azure-quickstart-templates/blob/master/quickstarts/microsoft.compute/vm-windows-admincenter/azuredeploy.json) – The Azure Resource Manager (ARM) template deploys Gen2 VM without enabling Trusted launch.
- [vm-simple-windows](https://github.com/Azure/azure-quickstart-templates/blob/master/quickstarts/microsoft.compute/vm-simple-windows/azuredeploy.json) – The ARM template deploys Trusted launch VM (without default as `securityProfile` is explicitly added to ARM template)

#### New behavior

By using API version 2025-11-01 or higher, Trusted Launch is enabled by default for new VMs and scale sets deployed if the following conditions are met:

- Source Marketplace [OS image supports Trusted launch](trusted-launch#operating-systems-supported).
- Source ACG OS image supports and is validated for Trusted launch.
- Source disk supports Trusted launch.
- [VM size supports Trusted launch](trusted-launch#virtual-machines-sizes).

The deployment doesn't default to Trusted Launch if one or more of the listed conditions aren't met, and completes successfully to create a new Gen2 VM and scale set without Trusted Launch.

You can choose to explicitly bypass the default for VM and scale set deployment by setting `Standard` as value of parameter `securityType` and using API version 2025-11-01 or higher. For more information, see [Can I disable Trusted Launch for a new VM deployment](trusted-launch-faq#can-i-disable-trusted-launch-for-a-new-vm-deployment).

#### Known limitations

***Unable to re-size VM or VMSS to un-supported Trusted launch VM size family (like M-Series) post default to Trusted launch.***

Re-sizing Trusted launch VM to [VM size family not supported with Trusted launch](trusted-launch#virtual-machines-sizes) will not be supported.

As mitigation, please register feature flag `UseStandardSecurityType` under `Microsoft.Compute` namespace AND roll-back VM from Trusted launch to Gen2-only (Non-Trusted launch) by setting `securityType = Standard` using available client tools (except Azure portal).

After a VM or VM scale set is created with Trusted Launch, you can't resize it to a VM size family that doesn't support Trusted Launch, such as an unsupported M-series size. To use an unsupported size, first deallocate the resource and change `securityType` to `Standard` by using Microsoft.Compute API version 2025-11-01 or later through a supported client tool. This operation isn't available in the Azure portal.

### Disable TLaD

To disable TLaD, unregister the preview feature `TrustedLaunchByDefaultPreview` under the `Microsoft.Compute` namespace on the virtual machine subscription. For specific VMs, you can bypass TLaD by setting the security type to `Standard`. For more information, see [Unregister preview feature](/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/preview-features#unregister-preview-feature).

Note

Azure portal, CLI, and PowerShell default to creating Gen2 VMs with Trusted Launch regardless of feature registration.

60	`ocid1.tenancy...`，而且 `oci setup config` 之後仍須在 Console 登記 API 公鑰。
61	
62	## SSH / homelab
63	
64	遠端首版支援 Ubuntu 24.04 LTS、amd64／arm64 與 systemd。管理使用 OpenSSH，
65	保留既有 host alias、port、identity、jump host 和 host-key 檢查。服務管理需要
66	root SSH 或可以非互動執行固定 Python helper 的 sudo；lazyclash 不保存 SSH 密碼。
67	
68	```sh
69	lazyclash vps register home --provider homelab \
70	  --ssh-host home-server --public-host proxy.example.net
71	
72	# 先檢查公開位址、端口、遠端環境與固定 artifact：
73	lazyclash servers deploy home-reality --host home \
74	  --recipe vless-reality --backend native --json
75	
76	# 帶回上一步實際顯示的 digest：
77	lazyclash servers deploy home-reality --host home \
78	  --recipe vless-reality --backend native --yes --expect REVIEWED_DIGEST
79	```
80	
81	`--public-host`／`--public-port` 是 client 連線端點；`--listen-port` 是主機的監聽
82	端口；SSH alias 可以指向私網。它們不需要相同。NAT 的外部轉發須另外配置，
83	Hysteria2 必須轉發 UDP。CGNAT、ISP 入站封鎖、DNS 或 router forwarding 不由
84	lazyclash 自動修正；部署成功和從 client 網路可用是不同結果。
85	
86	主機已有服務占用端口、同名 systemd unit／Compose project 或未知所有權時會停止。
87	新建且由 lazyclash 管理的 VM 可將 Docker 安裝納入計畫；既有主機選 Compose 時
88	要求已有可用 Docker Engine／Compose。預設 native 可減少常駐元件；不宣稱容器
89	必定比較慢。單服務的 1 vCPU／1GB RAM 是起點，實際吞吐、CPU 和記憶體需量測。
90	
91	## 協議配方
92	
93	| ID | 服務與入口 | 條件 |
94	|---|---|---|
95	| `vless-reality` | Xray；VLESS + TCP/RAW + REALITY + `xtls-rprx-vision` | 預設；不需要自有網域／憑證；REALITY target 從 VPS 驗證 TLS |
96	| `hysteria2` | Hysteria2；QUIC/UDP + TLS | UDP 可達、DNS 網域和憑證；沒有 TCP fallback |
97	| `legacy-vmess-ws-tls` | Xray VMess AEAD + WS、nginx TLS | 保留歷史 Azure 組合；需要網域、TCP 與憑證續期 |
98	
99	VLESS 是協議、TCP／WS 是傳輸、REALITY／TLS 是安全層、Vision 是 flow。
100	REALITY 須讓 Xray 直接處理連線，不能放在一般 HTTP CDN 或 nginx TLS termination 後。
101	Hysteria2 與 legacy 配方使用 ACME HTTP challenge，TCP 80 須可達，續期後重新載入
102	對應服務。首版不使用跳過憑證驗證、不自動配置 DNS provider、不啟用 port hopping。
103	Trojan／XHTTP 可作後續配方；目前未宣稱支援其部署／匯出組合。
104	
105	所有 binary 以官方 release SHA-256 驗證；image 解析成不可變 digest。
106	預設使用本版固定版本，`--version latest` 才追蹤上游；版本在預覽時具體化，不在重啟時浮動升級。移除服務不會解除安裝共用 OS 套件。
107	
108	來源：[Xray REALITY](https://xtls.github.io/en/config/transports/reality.html)、
109	[VLESS flow](https://xtls.github.io/en/config/inbounds/vless.html)、
110	[Hysteria2](https://v2.hysteria.network/docs/advanced/Full-Server-Config/)、
111	[Mihomo VLESS](https://wiki.metacubex.one/en/config/proxies/vless/)。
112	
113	使用者回報已驗證的是歷史 Azure + VMess/WS/TLS；DockerCompose-V2Ray 的
114	`9e6f3b957edbbaf2bbcfd9deea8d871873069e56` 另記錄了新 REALITY 配方的臨時 VM 測試。
115	這兩者與 lazyclash 實際測試結果分開，不能自動視為目前線路仍然可用。
116	[原始遷移與驗證紀錄](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/DockerCompose-V2Ray/blob/9e6f3b957edbbaf2bbcfd9deea8d871873069e56/docs/REALITY-MIGRATION.md)。
117	
118	## VPS 選型與費用
119	
120	以下是 **2026-09-21 查詢的報價快照**；按地區、庫存與帳戶條件重新核對，
121	不含稅、額外備份及其他資源。中國大陸線路需從自己的 ISP、地區與晚高峰實測。
122	
123	| 方案 | 資源與價格 | 流量與定位 |
124	|---|---|---|
125	| Oracle Always Free | 符合 home region／tenancy 累計額度時免費 | 10TB outbound；可能無容量或回收閒置 VM；優先檢查 |
126	| RackNerd special | 1GB／20GB SSD，$21.99／年；2GB／35GB，$35.99／年 | 廣告列 3TB／5TB 月流量；確認計量規則、年付與機房後走 SSH |
127	| Vultr | 1 vCPU／1GB／25GB，約 $5／月 | 1024GB outbound；多個亞洲 region；超額 $0.01/GB |
128	| Linode / Akamai | Nanode 1GB／25GB，約 $5／月 | 1000GB outbound；標準 region 超額 $0.005/GB |
129	| DigitalOcean Droplet | 512MiB $4／月；1GiB $6／月 | 500／1000GiB outbound；超額 $0.01/GiB；後者是均衡起點 |
130	| Azure | 查所選 region 的小型 B-series；VM、磁碟、static IPv4 分項 | `az` 自動建機；按完整固定成本排序，流量另計 |
131	| AWS Lightsail | 查所選 region 的 Linux／IPv4 bundle，至少 1GiB RAM | `aws lightsail`；固定月費，inbound＋outbound 共用 allowance |
132	| AWS EC2 | 查 T4g／T3a／T3 micro 等小型 burstable VM | `aws ec2`；compute、gp3、EIP、流量分項，CPU credits 使用 Standard |
133	
134	Oracle 只使用 Always Free A1 配方；目前保守限制為 tenancy 合計 2 OCPU／12GB
135	RAM、200GB boot/block storage，並查當月用量。免費額度、trial credits、配額和
136	實際機房容量分別處理；查不到必要資料就不建立，不會自動改用付費 shape。
137	未提供 subnet 時可建立帶操作標記的 VCN／internet gateway／route table／
138	security list／public subnet，不建立付費 NAT gateway。重用的網路保留原所有權。

175	[Lightsail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lightsail/latest/userguide/amazon-lightsail-faq-data-transfer-allowance.html)、

178	## Azure、AWS Lightsail 與 EC2
179	
180	以下命令都是唯讀查詢或建立預覽。執行前登入 Azure CLI／設定 AWS profile。
181	
182	```sh
183	lazyclash vps discover --provider azure --kind subscriptions --json
184	lazyclash vps discover --provider azure --subscription SUBSCRIPTION_ID --kind regions --json
185	lazyclash vps discover --provider aws-ec2 --profile personal --kind regions --json
186	lazyclash vps discover --provider aws-lightsail --profile personal --region ap-northeast-1 --kind plans --json
187	
188	lazyclash vps create azure-jp --provider azure --subscription SUBSCRIPTION_ID \
189	  --region japaneast --architecture auto --ssh-key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub --json
190	lazyclash vps create lightsail-jp --provider aws-lightsail --profile personal \
191	  --region ap-northeast-1 --ssh-key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub --json
192	lazyclash vps create ec2-jp --provider aws-ec2 --profile personal \
193	  --region ap-northeast-1 --architecture auto --ssh-key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub --json
194	
195	# 使用 discovery 回傳的實際 bundle ID；單位以 quote 輸出為準。
196	lazyclash vps estimate --provider aws-lightsail --profile personal \
197	  --region ap-northeast-1 --plan BUNDLE_ID --egress 500 --ingress 500 --json
198	```
199	
200	檢查預覽中的帳戶、region、AZ、固定映像、完整費用與 SSH CIDR。建立時使用
201	相同參數加 `--yes --expect REVIEWED_DIGEST`；若可用性或報價改變，重新預覽。
202	`vps create --interactive` 和 TUI 的 **Deploy → Create a cloud VPS** 提供同一
203	套選擇與 review。非互動命令省略 `--plan` 時，在所選 region 中解析至少 1GiB
204	RAM 的低成本相容方案；`--architecture auto` 同時允許 ARM 與 x86，不保證
205	任何型號有容量。ARM／x86 映像必須配對，preview 固定 Ubuntu 24.04 的版本／ID。
206	Lightsail 首版只使用已核實的 Ubuntu 24.04 x86 blueprint；Azure／EC2 可選 ARM。
207	可用 `--availability-zone` 固定 AZ；`--disk-gb` 僅供 Azure／EC2 調整根磁碟。
208	
209	`vps catalog` 也提供美東區域的固定費用快照供比較：Lightsail 1GiB IPv4 bundle
210	約 $7／月、EC2 T4g micro 加 20GiB gp3 與 IPv4 約 $11.38／月、Azure B2pts v2
211	加 32GiB Standard SSD 與 IPv4 約 $12.18／月。這些是 730 小時月份的起點，
212	不含流量、稅與 Azure 磁碟交易費；不同區域以即時 quote 為準。
213	[Lightsail 價格](https://aws.amazon.com/lightsail/pricing/)、
214	[EC2 On-Demand](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/on-demand/)、
215	[Azure Retail Prices API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/cost-management/retail-prices/azure-retail-prices)。
216	
217	| Provider | 建立的必要資源 | `vps stop` 的行為 |
218	|---|---|---|
219	| `azure` | 專用 resource group、VNet/subnet、NSG、NIC、Standard Static IPv4；預設 32GiB Standard SSD | deallocate VM；保留 disk／IPv4 費用 |

package vps

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestAzureSecurityValidationAndArguments(t *testing.T) {
	for _, r := range []CreateRequest{
		{Provider: "azure", AzureSecurityType: "wrong"},
		{Provider: "aws-ec2", AzureSecurityType: "TrustedLaunch"},
		{Provider: "oracle", AzureSecurityType: "Standard"},
	} {
		if err := ValidateDraft(r); err == nil {
			t.Fatalf("accepted invalid security mode: %+v", r)
		}
	}
	want := []string{"--security-type", "TrustedLaunch", "--enable-secure-boot", "true", "--enable-vtpm", "true"}
	if got := azureSecurityArgs(CreateRequest{AzureSecurityType: "TrustedLaunch"}); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("Trusted Launch flags: %v", got)
	}
	for _, value := range []string{"", "Standard"} {
		if got := azureSecurityArgs(CreateRequest{AzureSecurityType: value}); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []string{"--security-type", "Standard"}) {
			t.Fatalf("legacy/Standard flags: %v", got)
		}
	}
	r := CreateRequest{Provider: "azure"}
	before := digest(r)
	r.AzureSecurityType = "TrustedLaunch"
	if before == digest(r) {
		t.Fatal("security mode is not bound to request digest")
	}
}

func trustedLaunchFixture(t *testing.T, imageSupported bool) *azureFixture {
	t.Helper()
	f := newAzureFixture(t)
	f.s.options.Run = func(ctx context.Context, exe string, args []string) ([]byte, error) {
		data, err := f.run(ctx, exe, args)
		if err != nil {
			return data, err
		}
		command := strings.Join(args, " ")
		if strings.HasPrefix(command, "vm list-skus") {
			var rows []map[string]any
			if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &rows); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			for _, row := range rows {
				if row["name"] == "Standard_B2pts_v2" {
					row["capabilities"] = append(row["capabilities"].([]any), map[string]any{"name": "TrustedLaunchDisabled", "value": "True"})
				}
			}
			return json.Marshal(rows)
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(command, "vm image show") && !imageSupported {
			var image map[string]any
			if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &image); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			delete(image, "features")
			return json.Marshal(image)
		}
		return data, nil
	}
	return f
}

func TestAzureTrustedLaunchFiltersSizeAndValidatesImageBeforeWrites(t *testing.T) {
	f := trustedLaunchFixture(t, true)
	r := f.op.Request
	r.Plan, r.Image, r.Architecture, r.AzureSecurityType = "", "", "auto", "TrustedLaunch"
	resolved, _, err := f.a.Resolve(context.Background(), r)
	if err != nil || resolved.Plan != "Standard_B2ats_v2" || resolved.Architecture != "amd64" || resolved.AzureSecurityType != "TrustedLaunch" {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected resolution: %+v, %v", resolved, err)
	}
	r.Plan = "Standard_B2pts_v2"
	if _, _, err := f.a.Resolve(context.Background(), r); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("accepted a size with TrustedLaunchDisabled=True")
	}
	if len(f.writes) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("security preflight mutated the cloud")
	}
	f = trustedLaunchFixture(t, false)
	r.Plan = "Standard_B2ats_v2"
	if _, _, err := f.a.Resolve(context.Background(), r); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "image does not advertise") {
		t.Fatalf("unsupported image was not rejected: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestAzureTrustedLaunchProvisionAndSecurityVerification(t *testing.T) {
	f := newAzureFixture(t)
	// This fixture advertises no TrustedLaunchDisabled capability. The separate
	// real-world-shaped fixture above covers sizes that explicitly disable it.
	f.op.Request.AzureSecurityType = "TrustedLaunch"
	checkedFlags := false
	f.s.options.Run = func(ctx context.Context, exe string, args []string) ([]byte, error) {
		data, err := f.run(ctx, exe, args)
		if err == nil && len(args) >= 2 && args[0] == "vm" && args[1] == "create" {
			checkedFlags = true
			if azureFlag(args, "--security-type") != "TrustedLaunch" || azureFlag(args, "--enable-secure-boot") != "true" || azureFlag(args, "--enable-vtpm") != "true" {
				t.Fatalf("missing security settings: %v", args)
			}
			f.resources["azure-vm"]["securityProfile"] = map[string]any{"securityType": "TrustedLaunch", "uefiSettings": map[string]any{"secureBootEnabled": true, "vTpmEnabled": true}}
		}
		return data, err
	}
	if err := f.a.Provision(context.Background(), f.op, true); err != nil || !checkedFlags {
		t.Fatalf("provision flags=%v error=%v", checkedFlags, err)
	}
	vm := f.resources["azure-vm"]
	obj(obj(vm["securityProfile"])["uefiSettings"])["secureBootEnabled"] = false
	sp, _ := azureSpecFor(*f.op, "azure-vm")
	if err := f.a.finishResource(context.Background(), f.op, sp, vm); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "Trusted Launch") {
		t.Fatalf("security downgrade was not reported: %v", err)
	}
	if f.op.State != "cleanup-required" || cloudResourceOf(f.op, "azure-disk") == nil {
		t.Fatal("failed verification lost cleanup state or billable disk receipt")
	}
}

## 兩種安全模式是什麼？

### Trusted Launch：保護 VM 的「開機過程」

它主要提供：

| 功能 | 白話解釋 |
|---|---|
| **Secure Boot** | 開機時檢查 bootloader、核心與驅動的簽章，阻止未受信任的開機元件載入。 |
| **vTPM** | 虛擬 TPM 2.0，用來保存開機量測值及支援金鑰保護。 |
| **開機完整性驗證** | 配合 attestation 等功能，檢查開機鏈是否符合可信狀態。 |

**Trusted Launch 本身不額外收費**；這次貴約 US$1.10／月，是換成相容機型的價差。

它不取代防火牆、SSH 金鑰、系統更新或 HY2 的 TLS／密碼，也不是 Confidential VM，更不會自動保護所有應用程式秘密。

### `UseStandardSecurityType`：允許選擇 Standard 的訂閱開關

- `Standard` 是不使用 Trusted Launch 這組開機保護的 VM 安全模式。
- `UseStandardSecurityType` 是**訂閱層級的功能註冊**，不是 VM 規格，也不是代理協議。
- 你這個訂閱目前要求先註冊它，才接受明確的 `securityType=Standard`。
- 註冊不會自動把現有 VM 降級；它是允許後續操作選用 Standard。

Standard 並非完全沒有安全措施，仍可使用 SSH 金鑰、NSG、磁碟加密與 TLS。只是既然有便宜的相容機型，這次沒有必要放棄 Trusted Launch。**我沒有啟用這個訂閱開關。**

## 如果手動操作

### 推薦：新建 Trusted Launch VM

Azure Portal 建立 VM 時，選 **Trusted launch virtual machines**，確認 Secure Boot、vTPM 開啟，並使用相容的 Gen2 映像與機型。

用 `az vm create` 時，安全模式相關參數是：

```sh
--security-type TrustedLaunch \
--enable-secure-boot true \
--enable-vtpm true
```

其餘仍需指定訂閱、機型、映像、SSH 公鑰、磁碟及受限制的網路設定。

### 確實需要 Standard 時

以下是**替代方案的手動指令，這次沒有執行**：

```sh
SUB="<AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID>"

az feature register \
  --namespace Microsoft.Compute \
  --name UseStandardSecurityType \
  --subscription "$SUB"

az feature show \
  --namespace Microsoft.Compute \
  --name UseStandardSecurityType \
  --subscription "$SUB" \
  --query properties.state -o tsv
```

等狀態變成 `Registered`；若 CLI 提示重新註冊 provider，再執行：

```sh
az provider register \
  --namespace Microsoft.Compute \
  --subscription "$SUB"
```

之後新建 VM 才使用 `--security-type Standard`。這些操作需要相應的訂閱權限。

參考：[Trusted Launch 官方說明](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/trusted-launch)、[官方 FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/trusted-launch-faq)。

241	func exitIP(body []byte) (string, error) {
242		var result struct {
243			IP string `json:"ip"`
244		}
245		if json.Unmarshal(body, &result) != nil {
246			// Cloudflare trace is a newline-delimited diagnostic response. Require

248			count := 0

264	}

343					if s.Kind == "verge" {
344						if s.blockedGroups {
345							return d, errors.New("later Verge Merge masks groups needed to preserve node membership")
346						}
347						if !editCompanion(s.docs[s.groups], g.Name, desired) {
348							overrideCompanion(s.docs[s.groups], g.Name, desired)
349							s.Warnings = append(s.Warnings, "Group "+g.Name+" becomes a local override; subscription changes to this group will be masked and its display position can change.")
350						}
351					} else {
352						if e = replaceSeq(s.docs[s.base], "proxy-groups", g.Name, desired, false); e != nil {
353							return d, e
354						}
355					}
356				}
357			}
358			if len(wanted) > 0 {
359				return d, errors.New("selected destination group does not exist")
360			}
361		}
362		if e = s.refresh(); e != nil {
363			return d, e
364		}
365		return d, nil
366	}
367	func editCompanion(comp *yaml.Node, name string, node *yaml.Node) bool {
368		for _, key := range []string{"prepend", "append"} {
369			seq := get(comp, key)
370			if seq != nil {
371				for i, n := range seq.Content {
372					if scalar(n, "name") == name {
373						seq.Content[i] = clone(node)
374						return true
375					}
376				}
377			}
378		}
379		return false
380	}
381	func overrideCompanion(comp *yaml.Node, name string, node *yaml.Node) {
382		deleted := sequence(comp, "delete")
383		has := false
384		for _, v := range deleted.Content {
385			if v.Value == name {
386				has = true
387			}
388		}
389		if !has {
390			deleted.Content = append(deleted.Content, str(name))
391		}
392		if !editCompanion(comp, name, node) {
393			seq := sequence(comp, "prepend")
394			seq.Content = append(seq.Content, clone(node))
395		}
396	}
397	func validateGraph(root *yaml.Node) error {
398		proxies, e := proxyDefinitions(root, "")
399		if e != nil {
400			return e
401		}
402		groups, e := definitions(root, "proxy-groups", "group", "")
403		if e != nil {
404			return e
405		}
406		names := map[string]bool{"DIRECT": true, "REJECT": true, "REJECT-DROP": true, "PASS": true, "COMPATIBLE": true, "GLOBAL": true}
407		for _, d := range append(proxies, groups...) {
408			if names[d.Name] {
409				return errors.New("node/group name collides with another definition or built-in")
410			}
411			names[d.Name] = true
412		}
413		providers := get(root, "proxy-providers")
414		hasProviders := providers != nil

    sel=selectors.DefaultSelector(); sel.register(p.stdout,selectors.EVENT_READ)

    while time.monotonic()<deadline:
        if not sel.select(max(0,deadline-time.monotonic())): break
        line=p.stdout.readline()

        print(json.dumps({'path':label,'source_ip':ip,'vm_received_packets':incoming,'vm_reply_packets':outgoing}),flush=True)
    print('Header sample:')
    print('\n'.join(packets[:12]))
finally:
    if p.poll() is None:
        p.terminate()
        try: p.communicate(timeout=5)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: p.kill(); p.communicate()

因此，問題落在 **VM 送出回應，到 Mac 網卡收到之間**，而不是帳密錯誤或 Verge 收到封包後處理失敗。連很小的 UDP 回包也沒抵達，不太像單純只丟大封包的 MTU 問題。

### 能判定是 GFW 嗎？

**還不能。** 目前無法區分：
- GFW／ISP 的回程過濾；
- 家用路由器或 NAT 的 UDP 處理；
- 其他跨境回程路徑問題。

下一個最省事的對照是：**同一台 Mac 改接手機熱點，再測 `hy2-hk`**。先不需要重建 VM、放寬防火牆或更換帳密。

兩個節點與主代理設定都保持不變。本輪擷取已完成，請在那個終端按 **Ctrl+C** 停止；記錄檔可以保留供後續比對。

# project-knowledge-harness

A lightweight, file-based memory harness for any software project.

Three surfaces, sharply separated by **time direction** and **access pattern**:

| Surface | Time | Question it answers | Access pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TODO.md` | Future | "What might we do later?" | Read top to bottom (priority lanes) |
| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "What was the analysis behind this idea?" | Indexed from `TODO.md` |
| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptom keywords** |

Plus, in projects that already have agent contracts, `AGENTS.md` Hard
invariants answer "What rules MUST agents follow?". Pitfalls *graduate* to
Hard invariants when serious enough — see
[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).

## When to use this skill

Use this skill when the user surfaces any of:

- A long-term TODO list with no home, or a messy `TODO.md` that needs
  structure (signals: "where should ideas go?", "maybe later", "工程量太大需要再評估")
- A debugging session worth saving (signals: "keep solving the same problem
  twice", "save this troubleshooting", "踩過的坑", "TROUBLESHOOTING.md
  scattered across docs/")
- A request to consolidate `IDEAS.md` / `ROADMAP.md` / `WISHLIST.md` /
  `LESSONS.md` files

Do NOT use this skill for active sprint planning (use issue trackers),
ephemeral agent scratchpads (use `.claude/plans/`), or current feature
documentation (use `docs/`).

## How to apply this skill (default workflow)

The skill bundles five scripts and several templates. **Default to the
init script** for setup, and **default to `add-todo.sh` / `sweep-inbox.sh`
for capture** rather than asking the agent to edit `TODO.md` by hand.

```
scripts/
  init.sh         # one-shot setup of TODO.md + backlog/ + pitfalls/
                  # + agent guidance + README snippet
  todo-kanban.sh  # validate TODO.md format and render kanban-style board
  add-todo.sh     # insert a structured entry into the right ## P* lane
  promote-todo.sh # move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
  sweep-inbox.sh  # triage backlog/inbox.md into TODO.md via add-todo.sh
```

### 1. Run `scripts/init.sh` against the target repo

```sh
scripts/init.sh \
  --target /path/to/project \
  --project-name "My Project" \
  --deployment chezmoi   # or npm | pip | docker | none
```

The script:

1. Creates `TODO.md`, `backlog/README.md`, `pitfalls/README.md` from
   `assets/*.template`, substituting placeholders.
2. Appends an agent-guidance snippet to `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (auto-detected,
   override with `--agent-contract`).
3. Appends a "Roadmap & lessons learned" section to `README.md`.
4. Runs `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md` so any drift is
   caught immediately.
5. Prints the deployment-exclusion lines you should add manually (it does
   not edit ignore files — see
   [`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](references/deployment-exclusion.md)).

`init.sh` is idempotent: existing files are skipped unless `--force` is
given, and snippets append only if a sentinel marker is missing.

### 2. Mid-conversation, when the user surfaces a "maybe later" idea

Signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來", "not now but…".

1. If `TODO.md` doesn't exist yet, run `scripts/init.sh` first.
2. **Default path — call `scripts/add-todo.sh`** with the priority,
   effort, title, and description. This inserts the canonical line into
   the right `## P*` lane and re-validates. Add `--backlog` if the
   conversation produced enough investigation that a `backlog/<slug>.md`
   doc is worth scaffolding.

   ```sh
   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority "P?" --effort M \
     --title "Try Rspress for docs" \
     --description "Evaluate AI-native docs framework alternative"
   ```

3. **Quick-capture path — append to `backlog/inbox.md`** when the user
   isn't sure of priority/effort yet, or is mid-thought:

   ```sh
   echo "- $UNSTRUCTURED_THOUGHT" >> backlog/inbox.md
   ```

   Later (this session or next), run `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` to
   formalize the loose lines into `TODO.md` one at a time. The sweeper
   prompts for missing fields per line; in `--batch` mode it only
   processes lines that already have `priority=… effort=… title="…"
   description="…"` pairs and leaves ambiguous ones in place.

4. **Manual edit path — only when scripts can't help.** Use the syntax
   from [`references/tag-schema.md`](references/tag-schema.md) and run
   `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` afterwards.

5. If you wrote a `backlog/<slug>.md` (either via `--backlog` or by
   hand), make sure the TODO line ends with
   ` → [research](backlog/<slug>.md)` so the index points to the doc.

### 3. Mid-conversation, when you finish debugging something tricky

Signals: "phew, that took a while", "weird, the error didn't say anything
about X", "this is the third time we've hit this", or you find yourself
reconstructing context that isn't in any doc.

1. Create `pitfalls/<symptom-slug>.md` immediately from
   `assets/pitfall-doc.md.template`, while the trace is fresh. Title the
   doc by the **symptom**, not the root cause — you'll search by what
   you're seeing, not by what you eventually learned.
2. Copy verbatim error messages — never paraphrase, it kills grep-ability.
3. If the trap is severe (silent corruption / cross-machine recurrence /
   non-obvious workaround), surface it: "should this graduate to a Hard
   invariant in AGENTS.md?" — see
   [`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).

### 4. When implementing a `TODO.md` item

In the same commit:

1. Run `scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<what shipped>"`.
   It removes the active line and inserts the dated `Done` entry, then
   re-validates. It refuses to run if the substring matches zero or more
   than one active item.
2. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists, set its `Status: shipped` (don't
   delete — historical record may inform adjacent decisions).
3. If shipping uncovered a trap, write a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` for it.

## When a TODO entry needs a `backlog/` doc, when a debug needs a `pitfalls/` doc

Decision rules and the upgrade path to `AGENTS.md` invariants live in
[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md). Read it
the first time you set up the harness; consult it again whenever you're
unsure which surface a piece of knowledge belongs in.

## Tag schema

Two orthogonal axes, validated by `scripts/todo-kanban.sh`. See
[`references/tag-schema.md`](references/tag-schema.md) for the full schema,
useful tag combinations, and the exact validator-checked syntax.

## Anti-patterns

Common mistakes to avoid (e.g., spawning `IDEAS.md` alongside `TODO.md`,
titling pitfalls by root cause, paraphrasing errors). Full list in
[`references/anti-patterns.md`](references/anti-patterns.md).

## Deployment exclusion

`TODO.md`, `backlog/`, and `pitfalls/` are maintainer-facing repo metadata,
not files to ship. Cheatsheet for chezmoi / npm / pip / Docker in
[`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](references/deployment-exclusion.md).
`scripts/init.sh --deployment ...` prints the exact lines to add.

## Templates and bundled assets

- `assets/TODO.md.template` — `TODO.md` skeleton with example items per lane
- `assets/backlog-README.md.template` — `backlog/` index + when-to-add rules
- `assets/backlog-doc.md.template` — single backlog doc (context-first)
- `assets/pitfalls-README.md.template` — `pitfalls/` index + cross-reference
  table for traps documented elsewhere
- `assets/pitfall-doc.md.template` — single pitfall doc (symptom-first)
- `assets/agent-guidance.md.template` — snippet for `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`
- `assets/readme-roadmap.md.template` — snippet for project `README.md`
- `scripts/init.sh` — one-shot setup
- `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` — validator + Markdown kanban renderer
  (also supports `--json` and `--validate-only`)
- `scripts/add-todo.sh` — structured insert into `## P*` lane;
  `--backlog` also scaffolds `backlog/<slug>.md`
- `scripts/promote-todo.sh` — atomic active-→-Done move with re-validation
- `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` — triage `backlog/inbox.md` → `add-todo.sh`

## Reference implementation

A live example of this harness is at
[`daviddwlee84/dotfiles`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles):

- `TODO.md`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/` directories at repo root
- `AGENTS.md` `### Long-term backlog → TODO.md + backlog/` and
  `### Past pitfalls → pitfalls/` sections
- `README.md` `## Roadmap & lessons learned` section

1	# When to add a backlog or pitfall doc, and the upgrade path
2	
3	## Backlog: when an entry needs `backlog/<slug>.md`
4	
5	Add a backlog doc when **any** apply:
6	
7	- `P?` priority (record what was tried so it doesn't need re-investigation)
8	- Captures paused troubleshooting **that you intend to fix later** (preserve
9	  the error trace + root-cause analysis before context evaporates)
10	- Multiple options were considered (record trade-offs, not only the winner)
11	- `L` or `XL` effort (architectural; needs design before code)
12	
13	`S` items rarely need a backlog doc — a file path in the TODO line is usually
14	enough.
15	
16	## Pitfalls: when a debugging session deserves `pitfalls/<slug>.md`
17	
18	Add a pitfall doc when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something that
19	wasn't googleable, AND any of:
20	
21	- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (silent state, weird side
22	  effect, behaviour change without error)
23	- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
24	  must come after process completion, etc.)
25	- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
26	- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
27	- A specific tool version is required or forbidden, and failure at the wrong
28	  version is silent / confusing
29	
30	Skip a pitfall doc when:
31	
32	- Trivially googleable (next person solves in 30 seconds)
33	- Already covered as part of normal config docs in `docs/<tool>.md` —
34	  cross-link from `pitfalls/README.md`'s "Cross-referenced pitfalls" table
35	  instead of duplicating
36	- Already a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` — those have higher enforcement
37	  (cross-link only)
38	- One-off transient (network glitch, machine-specific config rot)
39	
40	## Disambiguation: pitfall vs backlog vs TODO entry vs invariant
41	
42	| Situation | Goes in |
43	|---|---|
44	| "We hit X, debugged it, applied workaround, moving on" | `pitfalls/` |
45	| "We hit X, debugged it, but the real fix is queued" | `pitfalls/` (capture trace) AND `TODO.md` (queue the fix) — link both ways |
46	| "We thought about doing X but deferred" | `TODO.md` (P2/P3) |
47	| "We thought about doing X, did a 2-day spike, deferred" | `TODO.md` (P?) + `backlog/` |
48	| "X is a rule everyone must follow forever" | `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant |
49	
50	## Upgrade path: pitfall → Hard invariant
51	
52	A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` (or the project's
53	agent contract file) when:
54	
55	- It recurs across machines / agents / sessions despite being documented
56	- The trap silently corrupts state (no error message, just wrong behaviour)
57	- The workaround is non-obvious enough that "remember to do X" is unsafe
58	
59	When graduating:
60	
61	1. Add the rule to `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants section
62	2. Link from the invariant back to `pitfalls/<slug>.md` for context
63	3. Leave the pitfall doc as historical record (don't delete — it explains
64	   *why* the invariant exists)
65
```

````text
1	# Pitfalls
2	
3	Past traps we've stepped on. **Symptoms-first** knowledge base — when a
4	problem recurs (on a new machine, after an upgrade, with a new tool combo),
5	grepping the symptom here lands you on the root cause and workaround in
6	seconds, instead of re-debugging from scratch.
7	
8	This folder is excluded from <DEPLOYMENT/PACKAGING MECHANISM, e.g. chezmoi via
9	.chezmoiignore.tmpl, Python via MANIFEST.in, npm via .npmignore> — it is repo
10	metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
11	
12	## Pitfalls vs the rest
13	
14	| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
15	|---|---|---|---|
16	| `docs/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
17	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
18	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
19	| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |
20	
21	A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant when the trap is serious enough
22	that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it recurs across
23	machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround is non-obvious
24	and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a `pitfalls/<slug>.md`
25	as historical record and link to it from the new invariant.
26	
27	## When to add a pitfall doc
28	
29	Add `pitfalls/<slug>.md` when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something
30	that wasn't googleable, AND any of:
31	
32	- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (silent state, weird side
33	  effect, behaviour change without error)
34	- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order"
35	- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
36	- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
37	- A specific tool version is required (or forbidden) and failure at the
38	  wrong version is silent / confusing
39	
40	## When NOT to add a pitfall doc
41	
42	- Trivially googleable (next person solves in 30 seconds)
43	- Already covered in `docs/<tool>.md` — cross-link from this README's
44	  "Cross-referenced pitfalls" table below instead of duplicating
45	- Already a Hard invariant (cross-link only)
46	- One-off transient (network glitch, machine-specific config rot)
47	
48	## File template
49	
50	See [`pitfall-doc.md.template`] in the
51	[`project-knowledge-harness` skill](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness)
52	for the per-doc template.
53	
54	Key sections (different from `backlog/` template — symptom-first, not
55	context-first):
56	
57	```markdown
58	# <Title describing the SYMPTOM, not the root cause>
59	
60	**Symptoms** (grep this section): <verbatim error messages, observable behaviour>
61	**First seen**: YYYY-MM
62	**Affects**: <tool/version/OS combo>
63	**Status**: workaround documented / fixed upstream in vX.Y / WONTFIX
64	
65	## Symptom
66	
67	Full error messages (verbatim — preserves grep-ability).
68	
69	## Root cause
70	
71	Why this happens, with source/docs/upstream issue link.
72	
73	## Workaround
74	
75	Copy-pasteable commands or config diff.
76	
77	## Prevention
78	
79	How to avoid stepping on this again.
80	
81	## Related
82	
83	Links to docs, sibling pitfalls, TODO entries, upstream issues.
84	```
85	
86	## Index
87	
88	Pitfalls owned by this folder. Keep alphabetical.
89	
90	| Slug | Symptom keywords | Status |
91	|---|---|---|
92	| (none yet) | | |
93	
94	## Cross-referenced pitfalls (still in their original homes)
95	
96	These traps are documented elsewhere and aren't duplicated here — the table
97	exists so grepping `pitfalls/` still finds them. Move into this folder only
98	if their original location stops being a natural reading flow.
99	
100	| Trap | Lives in | Why not here |
101	|---|---|---|
102	| (example: Tool X version Y bug) | `docs/tool-x.md` → "Known issues" | Already part of the tool's normal config narrative |

# HY2 直連 Timeout，但日本→香港鏈路成功

**Symptoms**: Hysteria2 / HY2、Timeout、HTTP 504、`installed-unverified`、`context deadline exceeded`、UDP 回程看不到封包、GFW / IP block / whitelist。  
**First seen**: 2026-11-01。  
**Affects**: 本次環境為 macOS、Clash Verge Rev 2.5.2／Mihomo v1.19.32（TUN 已啟用），Azure 香港 `eastasia`、Ubuntu 24.04、Hysteria `app/v2.13.0` 原生 systemd。這是此網路路徑的觀察，不宣稱所有版本／ISP 都有問題。  
**Status**: workaround 已驗證；直連根因未確認、暫停調查。使用者當前只需要臨時香港出口，不再擴大直連除錯。

## Symptom

在當前本機的兩個獨立測試節點上：

```sh
# 以實際本機 target／節點名稱替換；這會發出主動測試流量，但不切換 selector。
lazyclash --target local-clash-verge-rev proxies delay hy2-hk --json
lazyclash --target local-clash-verge-rev proxies delay hy2-hk-via-jp --json
```

直連節點的 CLI 錯誤原文：

```json
{"error":{"code":"rejected","message":"test proxy latency: controller rejected the operation or read-back did not match (HTTP 504)","operation":"test proxy latency","http_status":504}}
```

獨立 Mihomo client 綁定實體介面 `en1` 時也失敗：

```text
authenticated proxy HTTPS verification failed at the configured endpoints; server remains installed but unverified
```

client 日誌中的錯誤文字：

```text
error: context deadline exceeded
```

日本→香港節點成功，當次不同輪測得約 139–158 ms。此數字是節點延遲測試，不是吞吐量或長期 SLA。

## Root cause — 尚未確定

**不要把這個案例標成「已證實 GFW 封鎖 IP」。** 已定位到回程未在 Mac 實體網卡被觀察到，但沒有定位到攔截設備／業者。

### 已確認的證據

1. 香港 VM、HY2 systemd service、UDP 443 listener 與 certbot renewal timer 正常；公開 TLS 憑證有效。
2. 經日本路由的完整 HY2 認證／HTTPS 測試成功，觀察到香港 VM 的 public IPv4；server connection 記錄確認來源為日本節點，而非本機實體出口。
3. 直接從 VM 訪問兩個 verification endpoints 均得到 HTTP 200，因此不是測試網站一律拒絕這台 VM。
4. Azure **effective NSG**（不是只看宣告設定）確認：
   - TCP 22 的 `/32` SSH 管理白名單，不適用於 HY2。
   - UDP 443 對 `0.0.0.0/0` 開放，已套用 NIC／subnet。
   - IPv4 `AllowInternetOutBound` 先於預設 deny。
   - 額外 admin rule 僅限制特定 IPv6 出站目的地，與此 IPv4 連線無關。
5. Guest UFW inactive、iptables INPUT／OUTPUT ACCEPT、`net.ipv6.bindv6only=0`。
6. **2026-11-01 04:38 +08:00 的同一條 UDP flow，Mac `en1` 與 VM `eth0` 同步擷取：**

   | 觀察點 | 本機→VM | VM→本機 |
   | --- | ---: | ---: |
   | Mac `en1` | 10 筆送出 | 0 筆收到 |
   | VM `eth0` | 10 筆收到 | 22 筆送出 |

   筆數可能包含擷取重複，不用來推算丟包率。來源 port 在 NAT 前後一致；VM 回包包含 37／91-byte 小 UDP 資料，仍未出現在 Mac 的文字擷取記錄。

因此，此次 **不是我們把 HY2 誤擋在 SSH 白名單外**，也不是只憑本機 Timeout 猜測伺服器未安裝。VM 有送回封包仍不代表它們通過 Azure 邊界、跨境網路、ISP、家用 NAT 並抵達 Mac。

### 未確認的部分

- GFW、ISP／跨境回程過濾、家用路由器／NAT 或其他網路元件，各自仍是候選原因。
- 沒有在家用路由器 WAN／LAN 兩側擷取，不能精確指出丟棄點。
- 小回包同樣不見，不太像單純「只有大封包超過 MTU」；未做完整 MTU／分片測試。
- 未做手機熱點／另一 ISP、其他受控 UDP port、或不同傳輸設定的對照。不需要為臨時香港出口立即做這些工作。

## Workaround — 明確的日本→香港鏈路

保留原生 HY2 節點供未來測試；另建一個使用既有日本節點作 `dialer-proxy` 的 HY2 節點。兩者放在不影響主流量的 `HY2-Test` 群組。

```yaml
# 示意；使用 private inventory／export 取得真實值，不把帳密寫進此 repo。
name: hy2-hk-via-jp
type: hysteria2
server: HK_PUBLIC_IP
port: 443
[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]: [REDACTED:generic-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]]
sni: HK_CERTIFICATE_HOSTNAME
dialer-proxy: EXISTING_JP_NODE
```

- `dialer-proxy` 固定指向已驗證可承載 UDP 的日本**節點**，不要指向可能再選到此 HY2 節點的主策略群組，避免循環。
- 不關閉 TLS 驗證，不因為 Timeout 就放寬 SSH 白名單至全網。
- 日本只是前一跳；網站的連線對端通常看見**最後一跳香港伺服器的出口 IP**。須再確認 IP 地理資料庫是否標為 HK，不能只用 Azure region 當證明。
- 加入測試群組不等於一般流量已改走香港。Rule mode 下既有主 `PROXY` 可能仍是日本；只有實際選路到 HY2 的流量會使用香港出口。
- 多一跳會增加延遲，且日本、香港兩端可能各自計算流量費。網站仍可能使用登入帳號、cookie、GPS／定位權限、WebRTC 等其他訊號；IP 在 HK 不保證每個網站的地區判定。

本次 Verge source companion 匯入後，由使用者在原生 UI 重載 local profile，再用 `configs verify RECEIPT_ID` 核對 source／generated／runtime。不要繞過 owner 直接覆寫 generated YAML。

## Deferred next steps — 只有再次需要直連才恢復

1. 同一台 Mac 改手機熱點，重測原生 HY2；不要同時改密碼、port、VM 或策略，避免失去對照。
2. 如需定位家用 NAT／ISP，經授權後在路由器 WAN／LAN 與 VM 同步看同一 flow。
3. 必要時設計有明確界限的 UDP／QUIC／MTU 對照；涉及新 listener、firewall rule 或服務設定時先審核變更與回復方式。
4. 更新此文件的證據與狀態；沒有新證據時，不把候選原因升格成已確認根因。

## Capture / permission pitfall

在此非互動 CLI 環境，`! sudo -v` 失敗：

```text
sudo: a terminal is required to read the [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]; either use the -S option to read from standard input or configure an askpass helper
sudo: a [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] is required
```

不要收集對話中的密碼、改 sudoers 或換另一個 agent 繞過。改由使用者在一般 Terminal 自行啟動目標限定的 tcpdump，僅記錄文字摘要，看到 `listening on ...` 後才觸發測試；結束提醒 Ctrl+C。此做法不代表 agent 取得了其他 sudo 權限。

## Prevention / related

- 區分 VM running、service running、配置驗證、client 認證成功、特定路徑成功與地區判定；不能互相替代。
- 除錯副本只存權限受限的暫存目錄，輸出先遮蔽 credentials，完成後清除。
- 實際 endpoint 從本機 inventory 的 `azure-hk-hy2-tl`／`hy2-hk` 查詢；此筆記刻意不保存雲端帳號、訂閱 ID 或密碼。
- [Server deployment](../docs/server-deployment.md)
- [Diagnostics and routing](../docs/diagnostics-and-routing.md)
- [Proxies and groups](../docs/proxies-and-groups.md)

````

**日本 → 香港這條鏈路，已實測能呈現香港出口。** 網站看到的是最後一跳香港伺服器的 IP，不是前一跳日本的 IP。

兩個服務的結果一致：

- **出口 IP**：`HK_PUBLIC_IP`
- **IP.SB**：Hong Kong／`HK`，Microsoft Azure
- **Cloudflare**：`loc=HK`，節點 `HKG`

### 臨時使用方式

目前仍是 **Rule 模式、主代理走日本**，我沒有自動切換。要讓經 Clash 接管的流量臨時走香港：

1. 在 Verge 切到 **Global**。
2. 在 **GLOBAL** 群組選 **`hy2-hk-via-jp`**。
3. 用完切回 **Rule**，恢復原本的策略路由。

注意選日本鏈路版本，不是目前仍 Timeout 的 `hy2-hk`。

這是**香港 Azure 機房 IP**，不是住宅 IP。一般依 IP 判地區的網站會視為香港，但部分服務還會看帳號地區、定位權限、cookie，或限制機房 IP。

以下整理可直接放進自動化清洗腳本（如 `sed` / Python）或 `gitleaks`（Pre-commit 掃描工具）的 Regex 規則：

**1. 針對特定 JSON Key 的精準匹配（最推薦，零誤報）**

這組規則專門抓取 `az login` 或 Azure 設定檔中的敏感 Key-Value，適合用來做自動 Redact（替換）：

* **Azure UUID 欄位（攔截 `id`, `tenantId`, `homeTenantId`, `subscriptionId`）：**
  ```regex
  ("(?:(?:home)?[tT]enantId|subscriptionId|id)"\s*:\s*")[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}(")
  ```
  *替換字串（Replacement）：* `$1<REDACTED_UUID>$2`

* **Azure 預設租戶網域（攔截 `*.onmicrosoft.com`）：**
  ```regex
  ([a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]+)\.onmicrosoft\.com
  ```
  *替換字串：* `<REDACTED_TENANT>.onmicrosoft.com`

* **CLI 指令中的 Subscription 參數：**
  ```regex
  (--subscription(?:\s+|=))[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}
  ```
  *替換字串：* `$1<SUBSCRIPTION_ID>`

**2. 通用格式匹配（適合用於 Log 清洗或特定目錄掃描）**

如果你是要清洗一整段終端機輸出貼上到 Markdown 筆記，可以直接用通用規則一次替換：

* **所有標準 UUID v4：**
  ```regex
  \b[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}\b
  ```
* **所有 Email 地址：**
  ```regex
  \b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b
  ```

**3. 實戰配置：寫入 `.gitleaks.toml` 自動攔截 Commit**

如果你在專案中使用 `pre-commit` 搭配 **Gitleaks**，可以在專案根目錄的 `.gitleaks.toml` 加入以下自訂規則。這樣只要不小心把未去敏化的 `az` 輸出或設定寫進檔案，Commit 時就會直接被擋下來：

```toml
[[rules]]
id = "azure-context-ids"
description = "Detect Azure Tenant ID, Subscription ID, and Default Domain"
regex = '''(?i)(?:tenantId|subscriptionId|homeTenantId|"id"|--subscription)[\s:="']+([0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12})|([a-z0-9-]+\.onmicrosoft\.com)'''
tags = ["azure", "pii", "uuid"]

# 排除假資料或範例文字
[rules.allowlist]
regexes = [
  '''00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000''',
  '''xxxx'''
]
```

**日常快速去敏化小技巧（透過 `jq`）**
如果只是想在終端機把輸出貼給別人看，直接把輸出 pipe 給 `jq` 處理比事後用 Regex 替換更省事：
```bash
az account list | jq 'map(.id = "<SUB_ID>" | .tenantId = "<TENANT_ID>" | .homeTenantId = "<TENANT_ID>" | .tenantDefaultDomain = "<DOMAIN>" | .user.name = "<EMAIL>")'
```

# dev-cli

Git owns code; a dev task records a branch-backed change stream. Work items may
span streams and agent sessions; runtimes remain host-local.

## Discover what you need

Use leaf `--help` for syntax, `dev help <topic>` for workflows, and
`dev help --tree` for families. See [navigation](references/command-navigation.md)
for shortcuts, REPOS favorites/validated navigation and Try graduation/demotion;
dashboard details: `dev help tui`.
Prefer supported JSON. Read help before mutation: some actions apply immediately,
others require preview/apply. Do not preload manuals or run routine diagnostics.

## Preserve these boundaries

- Opening needs no task. Select direct, branch or worktree deliberately; use
  explicit `--base`. Managed worktrees stay outside repositories.
- Task-free worktrees use `dev git worktree create/open`; cleanup stays reviewed.
  `dev repo list --json` supplies navigation candidates, not external preferences/history.
- Choose `dev work start` for recorded park/resume/retirement; it prepares
  checkout/runtime. Agent launch is explicit; parallel writers need disjoint ownership and verified targets.
- Completion, artifacts, retirement and branch deletion are separate. Finalize
  after writer exit; retire externally. Use `retire --base` when integration is unproven.
- Cached/unknown observations, runtime `done` and merged PRs never authorize
  cleanup. Resolve guards; never improvise force removal or bypass checks.
- `dev pr checkout <URL>` is task-free; `--try` creates an independent clone.
  Provisioning is explicit; merge never cleans up locally.

## Read a reference for advanced operations

- Worktrees/lifecycle: [ownership](references/worktree-ownership.md), [lifecycle](references/task-lifecycle.md).
- Agents/prompts: [agents](references/parallel-agents.md), [handoffs](references/prompt-handoffs.md).
- History retention, exact sessions and co-commit: [artifacts](references/ai-artifacts.md).
- Cleanup: [retirement](references/agent-retirement.md), [triage](references/local-triage.md).
- Hygiene/scans/redaction: [hygiene](references/hygiene.md).
- Forks/setup/organization: [setup](references/repository-bootstrap.md), [bootstrap](references/bootstrap.md).
- SSH/fleet: [SSH](references/ssh-hosts.md).
- Dotfile setup, native chezmoi operations, or FLEET host actions: [dotfiles](references/dotfiles.md).
- Skill/MCP/instruction transfers, updates or removal: [transfers](references/agent-interop.md), [maintenance](references/skills-management.md).
- [Snippets](references/snippets.md).
- PR/MR pages, diffnav, gh-dash, checkout and merge: [pull requests](references/pull-requests.md).
- Recursive Git children: [submodules](references/submodules.md).

## Unexpected dev failures

Read [feedback and repair](references/feedback-and-repair.md). Preserve the
original task; extra investigation, repair, subagents and publication need
explicit consent covering scope and cost.
